name: Hostile rites (abhicāra) and their counter-rites
method_summary: The Atharvaveda contains spells against rivals and sorcerers and counter-spells returning a harmful spell (kṛtyā) to its sender; recorded here as a category only, without procedure.

warnings.text: Mīmāṃsā's standard example: the Veda describes the śyena rite for harming an enemy, yet such harm is not dharma — the rite is described, not commended (Śabara on Mīmāṃsā Sūtra 1.1.2, recalled with moderate confidence).
Vasiṣṭha's oath 'may I die today if I am a sorcerer' shows the gravity of the charge of sorcery.

notes: Summary only by design (treated as restricted: harmful rites; no procedure recorded).

name: Consecration as ācārya or sādhaka
method_summary: Ācāryābhiṣeka empowers an initiate to initiate and teach; sādhakābhiṣeka empowers one who seeks powers (bubhukṣu) to master a mantra.
alt_method_summary: Consecration by bathing with consecrated pots that confers the office of teacher (entitled to initiate and install) or of adept (entitled to master a mantra for powers).

name: Practice (abhyāsa)
method_summary: Repeated effort to hold the mind in stability (1.13), cultivated for a long time, without interruption and with devotion — with austerity, celibacy, knowledge and faith — so that it becomes firmly grounded (1.14, YBh 1.14); it opens the stream of discrimination (YBh 1.12).
signs_of_progress: not quickly overpowered by the impressions of emergence (YBh 1.14)

name: Practice and dispassion (abhyāsa and vairāgya)
method_summary: The restless mind is held by practice — bringing it back again and again to the self or to the Lord — and by dispassion (6.26, 6.35); the 'yoga of practice' by which one seeks to reach the Lord (12.9; 8.8).
notes: U05's contribution (the Gītā's formulation); the same pair in Yoga Sūtra 1.12 is given by U10.

name: Yoga of the inner self (Kaṭha)
method_summary: Realize the hidden god in the cave by the yoga of the inner self (KU 1.2.12); turn the gaze inward (2.1.1); restrain speech into mind, mind into the self that is knowledge, that into the great self, that into the peaceful self (1.3.13); yoga is the firm holding of the senses, when the five senses and mind stand still and the intellect does not stir (2.3.10-11); draw the thumb-sized person out of the body like the stalk from muñja grass (2.3.17).
signs_of_progress: the highest state: senses and mind still, intellect not stirring (KU 2.3.10)

warnings.text: 'Then one becomes undistracted, for yoga is arising and passing away' — the text warns that the state is unstable without vigilance (KU 2.3.11, one reading).
One who has not ceased from bad conduct, is not calm or collected cannot attain it (KU 1.2.24).

name: Recitation of the Āditya Hṛdaya
method_summary: Reciting the hymn to the Sun taught by Agastya to Rāma before battle, for victory and the removal of sorrow (Rāmāyaṇa, Yuddhakāṇḍa 105/107).

name: Attending to the initial and final points (ādyantakoṭinibhālana)
method_summary: Attending to the points where the breath arises and ends - the heart and the dvādaśānta - and resting there (Kṣemarāja's auto-commentary on Pratyabhijñāhṛdaya 18; compare VBT 24-25).

equivalents.note: same two points of the breath

name: Aghamarṣaṇa (sin-effacing recitation)
method_summary: Recitation of the Aghamarṣaṇa hymn (RV 10.190), traditionally while immersed in water, which removes sin as the horse-sacrifice does (MDh 11.261; GDh 19.12).
alt_method_summary: Reciting RV 10.190 ('ṛta and satya were born from kindled tapas …') while immersed in water or holding water, to efface sin, at the bath and in the twilight worship.

name: Agnicayana (building the fire-altar)
method_summary: The year-long construction of a great brick altar in five layers, typically in the form of a bird, within a Soma sacrifice; understood as rebuilding Prajāpati and constructing an immortal self (ŚB 6–10); the Śulbasūtras give its geometry. Its secret doctrine interiorizes it as fires built of mind and knowledge (ŚB 10.5.3).
prerequisites: prc:agnyadheya
alt_method_summary: The great rite of piling a bird-shaped fire altar of bricks in layers, opened by the verses on yoking the mind (VS 11.1–5 = TS 4.1.1), with the Śatarudrīya to appease Rudra and the Camaka at the stream of ghee; its meaning is expounded in the Brāhmaṇas.

name: Agnihotra (daily fire-offering)
method_summary: Twice daily, at sunrise and sunset, the householder who has established the sacred fires offers milk into the āhavanīya fire. The Brāhmaṇas explain it as healing the junction of day and night in Prajāpati (ŚB 1.6.3.36), as an offering of 'truth in faith' (ŚB 11.3.1), as a cycle of the oblations through the worlds into man and woman (ŚB 11.6.2), and as protection from retribution in the other world (ŚB 11.6.1).
stage: householder who has set up the fires (āhitāgni)
prerequisites: prc:agnyadheya

equivalents.note: ChU 5.24 calls the breath-offering the true Agnihotra

alt_method_summary: The obligatory morning and evening offering in the sacred fires, enjoined for life; Mīmāṃsā uses it as the example of an originative injunction ('he offers the Agnihotra') and of a name known from another text (MS 1.4.4).
Offering milk into the fire at sunrise and sunset, daily for life, by one who has established the fires.
notes: Procedure belongs to the śrauta manuals (U01/U02); only its Mīmāṃsā treatment is recorded here.

name: Fire offering (agnikārya, homa)
method_summary: Offerings into a consecrated fire in a prescribed fire-pit as part of daily, initiatory and occasional rites; for Vaikhānasas, the formless (amūrta) worship of Viṣṇu.
alt_method_summary: Offerings into a consecrated fire in which Śiva is invoked, part of daily worship and of dīkṣā.

name: The Agnīṣomīya animal offering
method_summary: The model animal rite of the soma sacrifice; in Mīmāṃsā the reference point for the question whether killing enjoined within a rite is sin (see dsp:sacrificial-killing).

warnings.text: The general prohibition 'one should not harm any being' stands; Mīmāṃsā and its critics (Sāṃkhya, Jains, Buddhists) disagree whether a ritual injunction exempts the act from sin.

notes: Summary only; no procedure recorded. Low confidence on the Mīmāṃsā references beyond the general debate.

name: The soma sacrifice (agniṣṭoma)
method_summary: The paradigm soma rite: the consecrated sacrificer buys the soma, which is pressed three times in one day, offered and drunk, with the chanting of the stotras by the udgātṛs and the recitation of the śastras by the hotṛs.
prerequisites: consecration (dīkṣā)

name: Establishing the sacred fires (agnyādhāna)
method_summary: The rite by which a householder establishes the three śrauta fires, after which the daily and seasonal offerings become his lifelong duty.
alt_method_summary: The rite establishing the householder's sacred fires, prerequisite to śrauta rites; its text names the three higher varṇas, which Ātreya uses to restrict eligibility (MS 6.1.26).

name: Agnyādheya (establishing the sacred fires)
method_summary: The rite by which a householder sets up his three Śrauta fires; the Brāhmaṇas fix its times by season and lunar mansion (the Kṛttikās, ŚB 2.1.2.3).

name: Purity of food (āhāraśuddhi)
method_summary: When food (what is taken in) is pure, the mind is pure; when the mind is pure, memory is firm; with firm memory all knots are loosened (ChU 7.26.2).
signs_of_progress: firm memory (dhruvā smṛti); loosening of all knots

name: Non-harming (ahiṃsā)
method_summary: Not injuring any being in any way at any time (YBh 2.30), kept as a great vow (2.31).
signs_of_progress: hostility abandoned in one's presence (2.35)
alt_method_summary: Lineage contribution (Upaniṣadic): non-injury among the priestly gifts of the life-sacrifice (ChU 3.17.4); not harming any creature except at sacred places (ChU 8.15.1).

name: The householder's daily round (āhnika)
method_summary: Waking at the hour of Brahmā to reflect on dharma, artha, bodily strain and the meaning of the Veda (MDh 4.92), purification, twilight worship, study, the five great sacrifices, work and meals with the breath-offerings, and evening worship.

name: The python's way (ājagara-vṛtti)
method_summary: Living without striving for food or comfort, accepting whatever comes and remaining still if nothing comes.

warnings.text: The Bhāgavata frames this for the sage who has given up striving; the text does not prescribe a fast but acceptance of what comes (U06 note).

alt_method_summary: Living like a python on whatever comes unsought, without striving for gain, content in pleasure and pain alike (MBh 12.172).

name: Ajapā-japa (the haṃsa / so'ham breath-mantra)
method_summary: Awareness of the breath's natural sound — 'ha' out, 'sa' in, 21,600 times a day — and its reversal as 'so'ham' ('I am He').
alt_method_summary: The breath itself utters the mantra: going out with 'sa', entering with 'ha', 'haṃsa, haṃsa', 21,600 times in a day and night; to be recognized as the japa of the Goddess, easy for the wise, hard for the dull (VBT 155b-156).

name: Consecrating the rosary (akṣamālā)
method_summary: Choosing bead material, threading with gold, silver and copper threads, and invoking the fifty letters a–kṣa into the beads (Akṣamālikā).

name: Meditation on the imperishable (akṣara-vidyā)
method_summary: Know the imperishable by the negations 'not gross, not fine, not short, not long...' and as that by whose command sun and moon stand apart; without this knowledge all rites are finite.
notes: Upaniṣadic 'vidyā' (meditation-knowledge); the Brahma Sūtra (3.3) discusses which vidyās are to be combined.

name: Meditation on the person in the eye
method_summary: Venerate the person seen in the eye as the self, the immortal, the fearless, brahman.

warnings.text: Virocana misunderstood 'the person seen in the eye' as the body and its reflection (ChU 8.7-8).

name: The food vows (Taittirīya)
method_summary: Do not despise food; do not reject food; make much food; turn no one away from your dwelling — each is called a vow (vrata) (TU 3.7-10).

name: Annaprāśana (first solid food)
method_summary: Feeding the child its first solid food in the sixth month.

name: Remembering the Lord at death
method_summary: Directing the mind to the Lord (Nārāyaṇa, Kṛṣṇa, Śiva) at the time of death, prepared by lifelong remembrance, since the last thought shapes the next state; the name uttered at death protects (Ajāmila).

warnings.text: Attachment at death leads to an according birth (Bharata's deer).

alt_method_summary: Lineage contribution (Upaniṣadic): 'O mind, remember what was done' (Īśa 17); at death take refuge in the imperishable, the unshaken, the essence of breath (ChU 3.17.6); meditating on Om until death (PrU 5.1); as one's resolve, so one becomes (ChU 3.14.1).

name: Remembering the Lord at the hour of death
method_summary: Remember the Lord at all times so that at death one departs remembering him (8.5–7); the yogin at departure, with unmoving mind, closes the gates of the body, holds the mind in the heart, sets the breath in the head (or between the brows), is established in concentration, utters Oṃ, the one-syllabled Brahman, and remembers the Lord (8.10–13).

warnings.text: Whatever state one remembers at the end, to that one goes — so practise remembrance at all times.

name: The inner fire-offering of Pratardana
method_summary: Recognizing that while one speaks one cannot breathe and while one breathes one cannot speak, one regards speaking as offering breath into speech and breathing as offering speech into breath — two endless offerings made continually, waking or asleep, in place of the outer agnihotra.

equivalents.note: both internalize the agnihotra into the breaths; the ChU form offers food into the five breaths

name: Inner and outer purity (Basava's seven restraints)
method_summary: Not stealing, not killing, not lying, not raging, not despising others, not praising oneself and not blaming others — Basava's definition of inner and outer purity.

name: Internal worship (antaryāga)
method_summary: Worship of the Goddess performed inwardly, held higher than external worship in the Devī Gītā's close.
notes: U06 contribution to a shared practice id.
alt_method_summary: Mental worship of the deity installed in the heart (and elsewhere in the body), with imagined offerings, before or instead of external worship.
Worship of Śiva in the heart with mental offerings before or instead of outer worship; the Tirumantiram makes the heart the sanctum and the soul the liṅga.

name: Antyeṣṭi (funeral rites)
method_summary: The dying āhitāgni goes out with his fires; the body is washed, carried to the cremation ground and burned (an āhitāgni with his sacred fires and ritual implements placed on his limbs), with the Yama hymn and funeral mantras; infants under two are buried; the relatives bathe and offer water, observe ten days' impurity, collect the bones, and later a funeral mound may be built (ĀśGS 4.1–6; YS 3.1–2; MDh 5.59–68; ŚB 12.5.2; 13.8; TA 6).

name: Final rites and ancestral rites (antyeṣṭi, śrāddha)
method_summary: Funerary rites for the initiate and rites for the dead (TĀ 24-25), whose purpose is to grant enjoyment or liberation to the departed (TĀ 1.318).

name: Anupāya: realization without means
method_summary: For one of the most intense grace, a single hearing of the teacher's word, or the conviction arising from scripture or reasoning, reveals one's ever-present nature; nothing further is to be done - no instrument and not even contemplation (Śivadṛṣṭi 7.5-6; TĀ 2).
notes: Abhinavagupta also calls it ānandopāya (low confidence on the alternative name).

name: Re-bathing in ash (anusnāna)
method_summary: Between the three ash-baths, after impurity from eating, sneezing, spitting, urinating or evacuating, he bathes again with ash, for purity and to show the sign.

name: Method of agreement and difference (anvaya-vyatireka)
method_summary: Reasoning that what persists when other things are absent (consciousness through the states) is distinct from what is absent when it persists (body, senses, mind); used by Sureśvara to separate self from not-self.

name: Non-possessiveness (aparigraha)
method_summary: Not appropriating objects, seeing the faults of acquiring, keeping, losing, attachment and harm (YBh 2.30).
signs_of_progress: knowledge of the how of births: 'Who was I? How was I?' (2.39, YBh 2.39)

name: Heedfulness (apramāda)
method_summary: Constant heedfulness, which Sanatsujāta calls immortality, as against heedlessness, which is death (MBh 5.42.4); with self-restraint and renunciation one of the three 'horses of Brahman' (11.7.19).

name: Image worship (kriyā-yoga, Uddhava Gītā)
method_summary: Worship of the Lord in Vedic, tantric or mixed mode, in an image (of stone, wood, metal, paste, painting, sand, mind or jewel), on prepared ground, in fire, sun, water or the heart; with love even water suffices.

warnings.text: Worship in images while despising the Lord present in all beings is 'offering into ashes'.

name: Posture (āsana)
method_summary: A steady and comfortable seat (2.46), achieved by relaxing effort and by coalescence with the endless (2.47); Vyāsa lists padmāsana, bhadrāsana, svastika, daṇḍāsana, sitting with a support, paryaṅka, the curlew, elephant and camel seats, the even configuration, and 'as is comfortable' (YBh 2.46).
signs_of_progress: the limbs do not tremble (YBh 2.47); no assault by the pairs of opposites (2.48)
notes: Vīrāsana appears in some editions' list of YBh 2.46.
alt_method_summary: Sāṃkhya contribution: posture is whatever is steady and pleasant; there is no fixed rule.

name: Postures of the Yoga Upaniṣads
method_summary: Lists vary: four chief postures (siddha, padma, siṃha, bhadra — Yogatattva, Dhyānabindu); eight (Śāṇḍilya); nine (Darśana); eleven (Varāha); seventeen (Triśikhi); siddhāsana and padmāsana are pre-eminent.

name: Observance of death-impurity
method_summary: For ten days (or by class) the sapiṇḍa relatives refrain from rites, study, certain foods and contact, ending with purificatory bathing (MDh 5.59–83).

name: Asparśa-yoga ('contactless' yoga)
method_summary: Gauḍapāda's discipline: realizing the unborn, controlling the mind without weariness (like emptying the ocean with a blade of grass), rousing it from dullness, calming distraction, recognizing latent attachment, not disturbing equilibrium, not relishing the bliss, until the mind becomes no-mind.

warnings.text: Yogins fear it, seeing fear in the fearless.
One should not relish the happiness arising in it; relishing is an obstacle.

signs_of_progress: the mind no longer imagines; no-mind (GK 3.32)

name: Duties of the life-stages and common duties (Vaiśeṣika)
method_summary: Following the four life-stages with pure intention, and the common duties — faith, non-injury, benevolence, truthfulness, non-stealing, celibacy, purity of intention, freedom from anger, ablution, pure things, devotion to a chosen deity, fasting, heedfulness — besides particular duties of class and stage.
notes: The list of common duties is recalled with low confidence.

name: Remembrance of the eightfold daily play (aṣṭakālīya-līlā-smaraṇa)
method_summary: Meditative remembrance of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa's pastimes through the eight periods of the day, following texts such as the Govindalīlāmṛta and Kṛṣṇabhāvanāmṛta, often in one's inner identity as a mañjarī serving Rādhā; given within a guru's transmission.
prerequisites: initiation
guru's instruction in the inner identity (siddha-praṇālī) in lineages that give it

warnings.text: The Gosvāmīs require eagerness born of grace and purification from offences; later teachers (Bhaktisiddhānta, recent) warned against premature imitation of this practice.

name: The eightfold daily service (aṣṭayāma sevā)
method_summary: Viṭṭhalanātha's ordering of the day into eight darśanas: maṅgalā, śṛṅgāra, gvāla, rājabhoga, utthāpana, bhoga, sandhyā-ārtī, śayana, each with its offerings, dress and songs of the aṣṭachāp.

name: Non-stealing (asteya)
method_summary: Freedom from desire for what is not one's own (YBh 2.30).
signs_of_progress: all jewels present themselves (2.37)

name: Asthisañcayana (collecting the bones)
method_summary: On a fixed day after cremation the bones are gathered into an urn, later buried or deposited in water (ĀśGS 4.5).

name: Cultivating the notion of the unlovely (aśubhasaṃjñā)
method_summary: Against the passion-producing notion of a body as a beautiful whole ('woman', 'man', with its attractive details), one cultivates the notion of its parts — hair, body-hair, flesh, blood, bone, sinew, veins, phlegm, bile, excrement and so on; as this is cultivated, lustful passion is abandoned.

equivalents.note: Buddhist contemplation of the unattractive (e.g. the parts of the body); similar content, different doctrinal frame (Nyāya affirms the self).

name: Horse sacrifice (aśvamedha)
method_summary: The royal rite in which a horse wanders for a year and is then sacrificed, with riddle exchanges and prayers for the realm; recorded as a summary only.

name: The Vedic Pāśupata vow of the Atharvaśiras
method_summary: A vow taken for life or a set term: after the virajā fire-offering the ash is taken and the limbs are touched and smeared with the Atharvaśiras formulae ('fire is ash ...'), the three lines are applied, and Śiva-yoga is practised at the three junctures.

equivalents.note: both are ash-observances named pāśupata; the Purāṇas distinguish this Vedic form from the non-Vedic Pāśupata scriptures

name: Honouring the guest (atithi-satkāra)
method_summary: Receiving a guest with water, seat and food, which the Atharvaveda equates point by point with performing the sacrifice; the Vrātya who knows is to be honoured above oneself.

name: Venerating it as the self
method_summary: 'One should venerate it as the self alone, for in it all these become one' — not as any single function (breathing, speaking, seeing), each of which is incomplete; venerate the self alone as dear (BAU 1.4.7-8).

name: Self-inquiry (ātma-vicāra)
method_summary: Inquiring 'Who am I? How did this world arise? Who is its maker? What is its material?' and discriminating the self from all that is seen; inquiry, not action, attains the Real.
alt_method_summary: Inquiring 'who am I, how did this world arise?' (Yogakuṇḍalī 3.27–29), and discriminating Self from not-Self (Tejobindu 5).

name: Self-knowledge supported by calm, restraint and celibacy (Prābhākara)
method_summary: Knowing the self as distinct from body, senses and cognition, cultivated together with calm (śama), restraint (dama), celibacy and the like; enjoined for non-return, it destroys the store of karma (Prakaraṇapañcikā). For Kumārila, self-knowledge removes the desire through which fruits accrue.

name: Self-offering to the Lord (atidāna)
method_summary: The 'supreme gift': giving oneself to the Lord, with prostrations while repeating the five mantras, instead of gifts of cows, land or gold.
signs_of_progress: non-return after reaching Rudra's proximity (as the text states the fruit)

name: Ātmārtha-pūjā (daily private worship of Śiva)
method_summary: The initiate's daily worship: bath with water and ash, twilight rites, bhūtaśuddhi, nyāsa, inner worship, worship of the liṅga with the five brahma-mantras and six limb-mantras, fire offering and japa.
prerequisites: samaya-dīkṣā at least

name: Purification of the self by restraints and observances
method_summary: Yama — the means of dharma common to all life-stages — and niyama — the particular observances — purify the self by removing demerit and increasing merit, as preparation for liberation.

equivalents.note: Nyāya takes over the pair from the Yoga śāstra without listing its members.
As above.

name: Seeing others' pleasure and pain as one's own (ātmaupamya)
method_summary: By comparison with oneself, see the same everywhere, whether pleasure or pain (6.32); see the self in all beings and all beings in the self (6.29).

name: Analysis of the three states (avasthā-traya-viveka)
method_summary: Observing that waking, dream and sleep and their objects come and go while the consciousness that knows them is uniform and continuous, and identifying with that consciousness.

name: Senseless speech (avitadbhāṣaṇa)
method_summary: He utters meaningless, repetitive or contradictory words.

warnings.text: Undertaken only after knowledge has been gained, impurity reduced and the teacher's permission obtained; the feigned acts must not conflict with the restraints (non-harming, celibacy etc.).

name: Senseless acts (avitatkaraṇa)
method_summary: He handles sticks, clods and the like as one who cannot tell pure from impure or fit from unfit, without breaking the restraints.

warnings.text: Undertaken only after knowledge has been gained, impurity reduced and the teacher's permission obtained; the feigned acts must not conflict with the restraints (non-harming, celibacy etc.).

name: Dwelling in the temple (āyatanavāsa)
method_summary: The first-stage practitioner lives in a temple built by another, under his teacher, as one lives on a riverbank.

name: Rites for long life (āyuṣya)
method_summary: Recitations and rites to hold back death and restore life-breath, keeping the person 'in the world of the living' (AVŚ 8.1).

name: The meditation taught to Bālāki
method_summary: Pass beyond venerating the persons in the sun, moon and other phenomena as brahman to the self into which the sleeper withdraws and from which all breaths, worlds and gods come forth.
notes: Upaniṣadic 'vidyā' (meditation-knowledge); the Brahma Sūtra (3.3) discusses which vidyās are to be combined.

name: The three locks (mūla, uḍḍīyāna, jālandhara)
method_summary: Root, abdominal and throat locks applied with breath-practice to turn the breaths upward and keep them in the suṣumnā.

name: Meditation on the self seated in the yoni (reported)
method_summary: Summary only: an opponent's one-line report that the Kāpālas attain nirvāṇa by meditating on the self as seated in the yoni. No further description is recorded here.
notes: Sexual rite category: restricted, summary only.

name: Meditation on the Lord in the heart-lotus (Uddhava Gītā)
method_summary: Seated evenly with gaze at the nose-tip, after breath purification with Oṃ, visualize the eight-petalled heart-lotus with sun, moon and fire in its pericarp and the four-armed Lord in the fire; meditate on each limb, then on the smiling face, then fix the mind in space and finally think of nothing, seeing the self in the Lord as light in light.
signs_of_progress: the delusion of object, knowledge and act ceases (11.14.46)

name: Service to devotees (bhāgavata-kainkarya)
method_summary: Honouring and serving the Lord's devotees regardless of their birth, which the teachers rank above service to the Lord himself; avoiding any offence against them.

name: The seven-day hearing of the Bhāgavata (saptāha)
method_summary: A formal recital of the whole Bhāgavata over seven days, modelled on Śuka's teaching to Parīkṣit, with vows for the hearers; the Māhātmya praises it above sacrifice, vows, yoga and meditation and tells how it freed the preta Dhundhukārī.

name: The twelve yamas and twelve niyamas (Uddhava Gītā)
method_summary: Practising the twelve restraints and twelve observances listed in 11.19.33-35.

name: Atharvavedic healing rites (bhaiṣajya)
method_summary: Healing by recitation of the hymns with plants, water, amulets, fire and the sun, touching the patient, and sending the disease away to distant places or creatures (fever, jaundice, leprosy, worms, consumption).
notes: Summary only; the Kauśika Sūtra gives the rite details (U02).

name: Bhakti-yoga: loving meditation (upāsana, dhruvānusmṛti)
method_summary: Daily, repeated meditation on the Lord (in one of the Upaniṣadic forms, the vidyās) as one's inner self, until it becomes unbroken, vivid as sight and full of love; supported by the seven aids and by duties done as worship, continued until death, with remembrance at the last moment.
stage: for those qualified by birth, learning and capacity (traivarṇika) after karma- and jñāna-yoga
prerequisites: the seven aids (sādhana-saptaka)
karma-yoga and jñāna-yoga leading to the vision of the self
signs_of_progress: vividness equal to seeing (darśana-samānākāra)
parabhakti, parajñāna, paramabhakti

warnings.text: It is long and difficult, obstructed by accumulated sins, and requires the last remembrance at death; hence prapatti is taught for those unable.

name: Bharanyāsa: the rite of laying down one's burden
method_summary: The formal performance of surrender, in which one places the burden of one's protection and its fruit on the Lord, with the sāttvika-tyāga; performed by oneself, by repeating after the teacher, or by the teacher on one's behalf.

name: Wearing the sacred ash and rudrākṣa
method_summary: Smearing tirunīṟu (in three horizontal lines) and wearing rudrākṣa beads as the marks of Śiva's devotee; praised as mantra and medicine.

name: Ash-bath (bhasma-snāna)
method_summary: Bathing the body in ash with the five brahma-mantras — the 'fire-bath' ranked above water-baths and enjoined for ascetics.
alt_method_summary: Smearing the whole body with ash prepared with mantras (Bṛhajjābāla; Bhasmajābāla; Atharvaśiras).

name: Lying in ash (bhasmaśayana)
method_summary: The practitioner sleeps and lies on ash.

name: Bathing in ash (bhasmasnāna)
method_summary: At each of the three junctures of the day the practitioner purifies himself, takes ash consecrated with the mantras and rubs it over the whole body while muttering, then enters the temple.
prerequisites: Pāśupata initiation

name: Inner worship with offerings of feeling (bhāva-pūjā)
method_summary: Worship of the inner liṅga of consciousness in the heart-shrine with inner offerings — forbearance as bath, discrimination as cloth, truth as ornament, dispassion as garland, samādhi as scent, freedom from ego as rice, faith as incense, knowledge as lamp, the world as food-offering, silence as bell.

equivalents.note: inner worship with mental offerings; here directed to the prāṇaliṅga and ranked above ritual worship

name: Fixing the gaze or breath between the eyebrows (bhrū-madhya)
method_summary: Shutting out external contacts and fixing the gaze between the eyebrows while equalizing the breaths (5.27); at death setting the breath fully between the brows with devotion and yoga-power (8.10).

name: The meditation on plenitude (bhūma-vidyā)
method_summary: Venerate in ascending order name, speech, mind, intention, thought, meditation, understanding, strength, food, water, heat, space, memory, hope and breath as brahman, each greater than the one before; then seek to understand truth, understanding, thinking, faith, steadfastness, action and happiness, up to plenitude (bhūman), where one sees nothing else; then the teaching of 'I' and of the self.
signs_of_progress: freedom of movement as far as each object reaches; the self-ruled moves at will in all worlds (ChU 7.25.2)
notes: Upaniṣadic 'vidyā' (meditation-knowledge); the Brahma Sūtra (3.3) discusses which vidyās are to be combined.

name: Purification of the elements (bhūta-śuddhi)
method_summary: Named in the Devī Gītā as a preliminary of daily worship (procedure not described here).
notes: U06 contribution to a shared practice id.
alt_method_summary: In Gauḍīya deity worship (Haribhaktivilāsa, following Pāñcarātra and tantric manuals), the worshipper purifies the elements of the body by meditation and places mantras on the limbs (nyāsa) before worship.

name: Purification of the elements (bhūtaśuddhi)
method_summary: In the preliminaries to worship the practitioner mentally dissolves the elements of the body, from earth upward, into their sources, burns away the impure body, and re-creates a pure divine body with mantras before placing mantras on it. Summary only.
alt_method_summary: Purification of the elements of the body by meditation and mantra before worship.

name: Contemplation of oneself as the reflection of Nārāyaṇa
method_summary: Seated upright during the purifications before worship, one contemplates Nārāyaṇa in the lotus of the heart and one's own self before him as his reflection, and prays: 'You are the original, I am the reflection, though there is a difference between us; flawless Lord, separate my faults from me.'
prerequisites: dīkṣā
ritual purity
signs_of_progress: removal of sin, according to the text
notes: A step within daily worship rather than a free-standing meditation; ritual details omitted.

name: Contemplating the body's impurity
method_summary: Reflecting on the body as a compound of bones, flesh, blood and impurities to loosen attachment (Nāradaparivrājaka 3; Maitreya 2).

name: The Upaniṣadic meditations (brahma-vidyās)
method_summary: Specific forms of meditation on Brahman taught in the Upaniṣads (such as the Dahara, Śāṇḍilya, Madhu and Antarākṣi vidyās), traditionally counted as thirty-two; each is a form of bhakti-yoga, chosen and practised according to the rules of the Brahma Sūtras' third chapter.
notes: The count of thirty-two and the list are recalled with low confidence.

name: Practice of Brahman (brahmābhyāsa)
method_summary: Thinking of Brahman, speaking of it, awakening one another to it and being wholly devoted to it; spending nights in reflection on the teaching of the Self.
alt_method_summary: Thinking of Brahman, speaking of it, instructing one another in it, and being wholly devoted to it — the constant practice recommended after knowledge dawns (quoted in the Pañcadaśī from the Yoga Vāsiṣṭha).

name: Vedic studentship (brahmacarya)
method_summary: Living with the teacher after initiation, tending his fire with fuel, wearing the girdle and antelope skin, begging, studying the Veda, in chastity and toil (AVŚ 11.5).
prerequisites: initiation (upanayana)
notes: U01 contribution: the Atharvavedic studentship. Other units contribute brahmacarya as celibacy (yama).
alt_method_summary: Restraint of the generative organ with the senses guarded (YBh 2.30).

Lineage contribution (Upaniṣadic): what people call sacrifice, offering, the long session, silence, fasting and forest-life is really brahmacarya (ChU 8.5); the brahma-world belongs to those who find it by brahmacarya (8.4.3); living in the teacher's house (ChU 2.23.1; 8.15.1).
signs_of_progress: vigour gained; the siddha can impart knowledge to disciples (2.38, YBh 2.38)

name: Brahmasambandha initiation
method_summary: The second initiation of the Puṣṭimārga, following the refuge mantra: the disciple, holding tulasī, dedicates body, senses, life, mind and possessions to Kṛṣṇa through a formula given privately by a Gosvāmī ācārya; thereafter everything is offered before use.

name: Riddle exchange (brahmodya)
method_summary: A ritual exchange of riddles about the cosmos between priests (e.g. at the horse sacrifice: 'who moves alone?' — 'the sun moves alone'), testing and displaying knowledge of hidden correspondences.

name: Service at the saints' brindāvanas
method_summary: Worship, circumambulation and vows at the tomb-shrines (brindāvanas) of Mādhva saints — above all Rāghavendra's at Mantrālaya and the Nava Brindāvana near Hampi — where the tradition holds the saints to remain present.
notes: Living practice described from general knowledge; no textual source checked.

name: The Cākṣuṣmatī vidyā
method_summary: Praise of the Sun for health of the eyes; one who knows it has no eye disease and none in his family is blind (Akṣi 1).

name: Recitation of the Devī Māhātmya (Caṇḍīpāṭha)
method_summary: Reciting the thirteen chapters of the Devī Māhātmya (with ancillary hymns in the recitation tradition), especially on the eighth, ninth and fourteenth lunar days and during the autumn Navarātra; the Goddess promises protection and prosperity to reciters and hearers (DM 12).

name: Cāndrāyaṇa (lunar penance)
method_summary: Summary only: an expiatory fast in which food follows the waning and waxing of the moon over a month (MDh 11.216).

warnings.text: To be performed only as prescribed expiation, with the observances and self-control the texts require.

notes: Restricted (prolonged fasting): no quantities recorded.

name: The seasonal rites (cāturmāsya)
method_summary: Offerings at the beginning of the three four-month seasons, including the Sākamedha with the Tryambaka offerings to Rudra.

name: The fourth prāṇāyāma (2.51)
method_summary: A breath-stilling that goes beyond the external and internal spheres, reached gradually after mastering the stages (2.51, YBh 2.51). Summary only.
prerequisites: mastery of the three kinds (2.50)
notes: Marked restricted as a form of breath suspension; no method given.

name: Courting dishonour (avamāna, paribhava)
method_summary: Hiding his sign and learning, the ascetic goes among people behaving so as to be despised and reviled; he regards censure as no censure. The text states that his demerit then passes to his revilers and their merit to him.
signs_of_progress: being thought mad or sinful by people (the intended result)

warnings.text: Undertaken only after knowledge has been gained, impurity reduced and the teacher's permission obtained; the feigned acts must not conflict with the restraints (non-harming, celibacy etc.).

name: Cūḍākaraṇa (tonsure)
method_summary: Shaving the child's head, leaving the tuft, in the first or third year (MDh 2.35).

name: Meditation on the small space in the heart (dahara-vidyā)
method_summary: Seek and understand what is within the small space in the lotus of the heart, in this 'city of brahman': as large as outer space, containing heaven and earth; the self free from evil, old age, death, sorrow, hunger and thirst, whose desires and intentions are real.
signs_of_progress: freedom of movement in all worlds; whatever one desires arises by intention (ChU 8.1.6-8.2)
notes: Upaniṣadic 'vidyā' (meditation-knowledge); the Brahma Sūtra (3.3) discusses which vidyās are to be combined.
alt_method_summary: Meditation on Brahman within the small space of the heart-lotus (Chāndogya 8.1); for Śrīkaṇṭha, meditation on Śiva as the supreme ether, his cit-śakti.

name: The three 'da': self-restraint, giving, compassion
method_summary: Practise the three that the thunder repeats — da, da, da: be restrained (dāmyata), give (datta), be compassionate (dayadhvam) (BAU 5.2).

name: Giving (dāna)
method_summary: Give because it ought to be given, to one who makes no return, at the right place and time to a worthy person (17.20); the gleaner's gift of his last food to a guest (MBh 14.92–93).
notes: U05's contribution to a shared practice.
alt_method_summary: Giving food and wealth to the needy, the friend and the priest; the gift at the sacrifice (dakṣiṇā).
Lineage contribution (Upaniṣadic): 'give' (datta, BAU 5.2); give with faith, grace, modesty, awe and understanding (TU 1.11.3); giving among the priestly gifts of the life-sacrifice (ChU 3.17.4).
Religious gifts - food, water, land, cows, gold, sesame and the sixteen great gifts - to worthy recipients at due times and places; gifts in life ease the road after death.

warnings.text: Who eats alone has only sin; the wealth of the non-giver finds no one to pity him.

name: Giving (dāna) in Vaiśeṣika ethics
method_summary: Giving and receiving as deliberate acts yielding merit, with rules regarding recipients who are superior, equal or inferior in merit.

name: New- and full-moon offerings (darśapūrṇamāsa)
method_summary: The fortnightly offerings of cakes and other substances at new and full moon, the model (prakṛti) of all iṣṭi rites; the White Yajurveda begins with its formulas.
alt_method_summary: The fortnightly Śrauta offerings of cakes and other oblations, entered with a vow of truth (ŚB 1.1.1.4–5), which heal the joints of the year-Prajāpati at the moon's phases (ŚB 1.6.3.36).
The archetypal iṣṭi (prakṛti), all of whose subsidiaries (e.g. the prayājas) are taught in its own context, from which ectypal offerings take their procedure; enjoined for one desiring heaven.

name: Dāsōha — sharing the fruit of work
method_summary: Giving what one earns by kāyaka to the jaṅgamas and the community in the spirit 'I am your servant'; in the modern maṭhas, free feeding and schooling.

name: Kuṇḍalinī yoga of the Devī Gītā
method_summary: Summary only: after the eight limbs, the Goddess describes breath control, the channels and six centres, and the rousing of kuṇḍalinī from the root centre to union with the supreme at the crown; procedures, counts and retentions are not recorded here.

warnings.text: The Devī Gītā places this yoga after the yamas and niyamas and within devotion to the Goddess; the text is to be taught only to the qualified.

prerequisites: the ten yamas and ten niyamas
a qualified teacher

name: The ten yamas and ten niyamas (Devī Gītā)
method_summary: Practising the ten restraints and ten observances listed by the Goddess as the first limbs of yoga.

name: Concentration (dhāraṇā)
method_summary: Binding the mind to one place — navel wheel, heart-lotus, light in the head, tip of the nose or tongue, or an external object (3.1, YBh 3.1).
prerequisites: fitness from prāṇāyāma (2.53)
alt_method_summary: Lineage contribution (Upaniṣadic): yoga as 'the firm holding (dhāraṇā) of the senses' (KU 2.3.11); fourth limb in MaiU 6.18; 'its further concentration' at the palate (MaiU 6.20).
Sāṃkhya contribution: concentration, with posture and one's own duty, accomplishes meditation (SS 3.32); with meditation, practice and dispassion it stops the coloring of puruṣa (SS 6.29).

name: Inquiry into dharma (dharma-jijñāsā, vedārtha-vicāra)
method_summary: Systematic investigation of the Vedic sentences by the adhikaraṇa method — subject, doubt, connection, prima facie view, conclusion — undertaken after Vedic study, before the student returns home, to know dharma for performance.
prerequisites: completed study of one's Vedic recension

name: Meditation (dhyāna)
method_summary: The continuous flow of a single cognition on the place of concentration (3.2); it removes the gross activities of the afflictions (2.11).
alt_method_summary: Lineage contribution (Upaniṣadic): venerate meditation as brahman (ChU 7.6); by the yoga of meditation the sages saw God's power (ŚU 1.3); the friction of meditation with Om (ŚU 1.14); 'meditating, one sees him' (MuU 3.1.8); a limb in MaiU 6.18.

name: Dhyāna: visualization in the āṇava means
method_summary: Āṇava immersion through meditative visualization, e.g. of the circle of the powers of consciousness in the heart (TĀ 5).

name: The Gītā's meditation (dhyāna-yoga, BhG 6.10–32)
method_summary: In solitude, alone, with mind and body controlled and without possessions, sit on a firm seat in a clean place; with body, head and neck erect and still and the gaze as if at the tip of the nose, serene and fearless, keeping the vow of celibacy, make the mind one-pointed, fixed on the self or on the Lord; gradually still the mind by a steady intellect and think of nothing else; whenever the restless mind wanders, bring it back; be moderate in food, sleep and effort.
stage: the one who has ascended (6.3–4); practised with determination and without despair (6.23)
prerequisites: renunciation of intention (6.2); self-control; moderation (6.16–17)
signs_of_progress: the mind steady like a lamp in a windless place (6.19); contentment in the self and happiness beyond the senses (6.20–21); the happiness of contact with Brahman (6.28); seeing the self in all and all in the self (6.29)

warnings.text: Yoga is not for one who eats too much or not at all, sleeps too much or too little.
The mind is restless; it is restrained by practice and dispassion.

name: Dīkṣā (consecration for sacrifice)
method_summary: Before a Soma sacrifice the sacrificer is consecrated in a hut with vows of fasting and restraint; the priests make him an embryo again (AB 1.3); he is born anew at the final bath.
alt_method_summary: The guru, after preliminary purifications and worship of the deity on a maṇḍala and in the fire, performs on the disciple a rite that acts on the soul (not caste or body): in the Śaiva form it binds the disciple to the observances (samaya-dīkṣā) and, in the liberating initiation (nirvāṇa-dīkṣā), purifies the six paths and destroys the bonds through mantra-power; consecrations of sādhaka and ācārya may follow. Pāñcarātra initiation admits to Bhagavān's mantras and worship.

The guru, having become Śiva by ritual identification, removes or burns the disciple's bonds by mantra-power (Sanskrit manuals), or initiates by look, touch, word, thought, scripture, yoga or fire (Tamil).
prerequisites: the descent of power (śaktipāta), shown by devotion (Kiraṇa 5); a qualified guru

warnings.text: For the capable the observances remain binding; knowingly breaking them is a great fault.

name: Initiation (dīkṣā) into Hari's worship
method_summary: The ācārya initiates a qualified devotee who has undergone the saṃskāras: the disciple sips the Lord's foot-water, receives mantra and vows, and thereafter worships; the Kṛṣṇāmṛtamahārṇava calls those without Hari's initiation 'beasts among men'.
prerequisites: devotion
saṃskāras
a qualified ācārya
notes: Ritual particulars (maṇḍala, fasting days) deliberately summarized, not listed.

name: Consecration of the sacrificer (dīkṣā)
method_summary: The consecration before the soma rite: the sacrificer is shaved, bathed, clothed anew, restricted in food and speech and kept apart, and so 'reborn' fit for the gods; 'here I go from untruth to truth' (VS 1.5) is the vow-taker's formula.

warnings.text: The dietary restrictions of the consecration are ritual observances within the rite; they are not recorded here in detail.

name: Initiation (dīkṣā) in the Trika
method_summary: Initiation in its many forms - samaya, putraka, abbreviated, by the balance, of the absent and the dead - purifying the paths (adhvan) and removing the bonds; the teacher observes signs of immersion in the disciple (ānanda, udbhava, kampa, nidrā, ghūrṇi; MVT 11.35). For one who knows the Heart, initiation needs no oblation (Parātrīśikā 25).

name: Pilgrimage to the divine sites and maṅgaḷāśāsana
method_summary: Visiting the temples sung by the Āḻvārs and praying for the Lord's welfare there, as the Āḻvārs and teachers did.

name: Recitation of the Divya Prabandham
method_summary: Recitation of the Āḻvārs' hymns in temples and homes — daily selections (nityānusandhānam), the annual festival of recitation (adhyayana-utsava) and the sung and enacted araiyar service — as the Tamil Veda.

name: Seeing the faults (doṣa-darśana)
method_summary: Reflecting on the faults in acquiring, guarding and losing objects, in attachment, and in the harm enjoyment does to beings, so that passion subsides; passion is not quieted by enjoyment but by seeing the faults of both.

warnings.text: Abstaining from objects for these faults is only a contentment, not liberation, without knowledge of the principles.

name: Discrimination of seer and seen (dṛg-dṛśya-viveka)
method_summary: Tracing the chain of seer and seen — object seen by eye, eye by mind, mind by witness — to the seer that is never seen.

name: The bull-sound (ḍuṇḍuṅkāra / huḍukkāra)
method_summary: A holy sound like a bull's bellow produced by touching the tongue-tip to the palate, made as part of the offering.

name: Constant recollection of the dvaya
method_summary: Reciting the dvaya with its meaning — refuge at the feet of Nārāyaṇa with Śrī, and prayer for service — throughout life, as the Lord bade Rāmānuja in the Śaraṇāgati Gadya.

name: Living alone (ekacaryā)
method_summary: The sage wanders alone, homeless and unobtrusive, because many people cause quarrel and even two cause talk.

name: Ekādaśī fast
method_summary: Fasting on the eleventh lunar day of both fortnights as the 'vow of Nārāyaṇa's day', with rules for days overlapped by the tenth (fast on the twelfth instead) and for the time of breaking the fast. A one-day fast, not a prolonged one.
duration: one lunar day, broken on the following day
notes: The texts' own exemptions (for the sick, aged, etc.) were not checked; no warnings recorded.
alt_method_summary: Fasting on the eleventh lunar day, named among the causes of devotion to Rāma.
Fasting from grains (or fully) on the eleventh lunar day, with extra hearing and chanting; obligatory for Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇavas (Haribhaktivilāsa).
Fasting and worship of Viṣṇu on the eleventh lunar day of each fortnight, with vigil and breaking of the fast on the twelfth.
Abstaining from grain (or food) on the eleventh lunar day as an observance pleasing to the Lord. Summary only.
alt_notes: U06 contributes only this source; details belong to the Purāṇa units.

name: One-pointed worship of Nārāyaṇa (ekānta-bhakti)
method_summary: Exclusive devotion to Nārāyaṇa, worship according to rule without desire for fruit, non-violence, self-restraint and knowledge of the self, by which the devotee goes directly to Vāsudeva (MBh 12.336).

name: Practice on a single principle (ekatattva-abhyāsa)
method_summary: Holding the mind to one principle to counter the obstacles and their accompaniments (1.32, YBh 1.32).

name: One garment or none
method_summary: He wears a single garment, or goes naked.

name: Concentrations (dhāraṇā) in the Mokṣadharma's yoga
method_summary: The Mokṣadharma's yoga teaches fixing the mind in concentrations (dhāraṇā) — on the elements and within the body — with the steadiness of an arrow-maker intent on his arrow, by which the yogin gains yoga-power (MBh 12.289; 12.298–306).

warnings.text: The path of yoga is described as hard and dangerous (the images and verses to be confirmed).

notes: Low confidence on the specific objects and similes; to be extracted in Phase D.

name: The five element concentrations (pañca-dhāraṇā)
method_summary: Holding breath and mind in five regions of the body, each with its element, shape, colour, seed-syllable and deity (Brahmā, Viṣṇu/Nārāyaṇa, Rudra, Īśvara, Sadāśiva; in the Triśikhi the four vyūhas and Vāsudeva); each conquers its element. Durations omitted.
signs_of_progress: mastery of the element: not harmed by earth, water, fire, air; moving in space (Yogatattva 83–102)

name: The five most potent limbs of devotion
method_summary: Serving the deity with faith, relishing the Bhāgavata with the like-minded, association with advanced devotees, congregational chanting of the name, and residence in Mathurā/Vraja; even slight contact with them awakens love.

name: Five kinds of withdrawal (pratyāhāra)
method_summary: Forcibly withdrawing the senses; seeing all that is seen as the Self; offering the fruits of acts; turning from all objects; and moving/holding the breath through the eighteen vital points (Darśana 7; Śāṇḍilya 1.69); the Yogatattva's withdrawal is regarding all perceived as the Self.

name: The fivefold Śiva-sacrifice
method_summary: Austerity as drying the body for Śiva, action as Śiva's worship, japa as the five syllables or praṇava, meditation, and knowledge as the meaning of the Śiva Āgamas — each replacing its Vedic counterpart.

name: Cultivating the four attitudes (maitrī, karuṇā, muditā, upekṣā)
method_summary: Cultivating friendliness toward the happy, compassion toward the suffering, gladness toward the virtuous and equanimity toward the non-virtuous, so that white dharma arises and the mind becomes clear and steady (1.33, YBh 1.33); saṃyama on the first three gives strengths (3.23).
signs_of_progress: clarity of mind (citta-prasādana); strengths of friendliness etc. (3.23)

warnings.text: Equanimity toward the wicked is not a cultivation; no samādhi and no strength come from it.

equivalents.note: Same four attitudes and 'vihāra' vocabulary (YBh 4.10) as the Buddhist brahmavihāras; objects and aim differ (YS 1.33 assigns each to a class of object)

name: Cultivating the four gatekeepers
method_summary: Cultivating peace, inquiry, contentment and the company of the holy — all four, or at least one with full effort, since the others follow.

name: Bhīṣma's fourfold meditation (dhyāna-yoga)
method_summary: The sage, seated, withdraws the senses and repeatedly steadies the wandering mind; in the first meditation reflection, reasoning and discrimination arise; persevering without despair he reaches the happiness of nirvāṇa (MBh 12.188).

name: Procreation rites (BAU 6.4)
method_summary: Lineage contribution (Upaniṣadic): BAU 6.4 treats marital union as a sacrificial act with rites for conception and offspring. Recorded as a summary only (sexual rite).
notes: Summary only under the restricted-content rule; no procedures, formulas or details reproduced.
alt_method_summary: The rite performed by the husband at the proper time for conception, first of the bodily sacraments (MDh 2.26–27; YS 1.11).

name: Gauḍīya initiation (dīkṣā)
method_summary: After mutual examination, the guru gives the disciple the Kṛṣṇa mantras (the eighteen-syllable gopāla-mantra and the kāma-gāyatrī, among others), tilaka and neck-beads; initiation makes one fit for deity worship. The mantras are given privately and are not recorded here.

name: Śrāddha at Gayā
method_summary: Offering piṇḍas at Gayā's sacred spots in sequence for the release of the ancestors.

name: Repetition of the Gāyatrī (Sāvitrī)
method_summary: Repeating the Sāvitrī verse to Savitṛ ('we meditate on that excellent radiance … may he impel our thoughts'), preceded by Oṃ and bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ, at the twilights; it is imparted by the teacher at initiation.
prerequisites: initiation (upanayana) in the tradition's own rules
notes: The rules of who may recite it and how often belong to the gṛhya and dharma literature (U02).
alt_method_summary: Recitation of the Sāvitrī verse preceded by Oṃ and the three utterances, especially at the twilights (MDh 2.76–78; YS 1.22–25).

name: Meditation on the Gāyatrī
method_summary: Venerate the Gāyatrī as all this — speech, earth, body, heart — whose four feet are the worlds, the Vedas, the breaths and the sun; and the space within the heart as identical with the space outside (ChU 3.12; BAU 5.14).

name: Dense recitation (ghanapāṭha)
method_summary: The most elaborate commonly practised recitation (ab ba abc cba abc, bc cb bcd dcb bcd …), whose master is called ghanapāṭhin.

name: The meditation seat and posture of the Gītā
method_summary: A firm seat of one's own in a clean place, neither too high nor too low, spread with kuśa grass, a deerskin and cloth; sitting there, hold body, head and neck erect, motionless and steady.
notes: The order of the layers (cloth, skin, grass) is read differently by commentators.

name: Study and hearing of the Gītā
method_summary: Studying the dialogue is worship of the Lord by the sacrifice of knowledge; hearing it with faith and without cavil brings the worlds of the righteous; teaching it to devotees is the dearest service (18.68–71).

warnings.text: It is not to be told to one without austerity or devotion, who does not wish to hear, or who speaks ill of the Lord.

name: Song as offering (gīta)
method_summary: Singing of the Lord's qualities and deeds, following the rules of music.

name: The gift of the Vaitaraṇī cow
method_summary: Giving a (dark) cow to a brahmin at or before death so that the dead may cross the Vaitaraṇī by boat.

name: Recitation of the Gopāla mantra
method_summary: Worship and recitation of Kṛṣṇa's five-part mantra with meditation on his form (Gopālapūrvatāpanī).

name: Keeping the vow hidden (gūḍhavrata)
method_summary: He keeps his knowledge, austerity, vow and mantras concealed.

name: Worship of Hari with qualities according to fitness
method_summary: Meditative worship (upāsanā) of Hari under the qualities fit for the worshipper: Brahmā with all qualities, humans as bliss (ānanda), knower (jña) and the ever-existing Self (sadātmā); the gods are liberated when Hari becomes directly perceived through such worship.

warnings.text: A person who desires what he is unfit for surely falls; serve Viṣṇu according to your fitness.

name: Seeing that the guṇas act: non-doership
method_summary: Knowing that the guṇas act upon the guṇas (3.28) and that the senses move among their objects, the knower of truth thinks 'I do nothing at all' (5.8–9); he sits as one indifferent, knowing 'the guṇas are acting' (14.23), and sees prakṛti as the doer and the self as non-doer (13.29).

name: Devotion to the teacher (guru-bhakti)
method_summary: Hold the highest devotion to God and to one's teacher as to God (ŚU 6.23); honour the teacher as a god (TU 1.11.2); the pupils worship Pippalāda as the father who takes them across (PrU 6.8).

name: Meditation on the guru's form
method_summary: Meditating on the guru's form, the root of meditation, often visualized in the lotus of the head at dawn (Devī Gītā 7.40.1).

name: Recitation of the Guru Gītā
method_summary: Reciting or chanting the Guru Gītā, prescribed in the text for success, protection and liberation at death; in recent times chanted daily in Muktananda's ashrams.

warnings.text: Not to be taught to the faithless, the deceiver or the hypocrite.

name: Service of the teacher
method_summary: Serving and worshipping the teacher as the Lord in body, speech and mind; in the Guru Gītā the guru's satisfaction fulfils all practices.

name: Approaching a teacher with fuel in hand
method_summary: Having become disgusted with the worlds won by action, go 'fuel in hand' to a teacher learned in the Veda and established in brahman (MuU 1.2.12); live with the teacher a set time in austerity, celibacy and faith before asking (PrU 1.2); serve the teacher (ChU 4.4-9, 8.7-12, 8.15).

name: Approaching the teacher (gurūpasatti)
method_summary: Approaching, 'fuel in hand', a teacher learned in scripture and established in Brahman, with humility, service and questioning, and receiving the teaching repeatedly until it is grasped.

name: Surrender to the guru (gurūpasatti)
method_summary: The fifth means of the Nimbārka school: complete dependence on the guru, who then performs the means on the disciple's behalf.

name: The Hare Kṛṣṇa mahāmantra
method_summary: The sixteen names 'hare kṛṣṇa hare kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa hare hare / hare rāma hare rāma rāma rāma hare hare' (the Kalisantaraṇa gives the Hare Rāma half first), chanted in japa or sung in kīrtana; the Upaniṣad states there are no rules of time, place or purity for it.

name: Recitation of the sixteen names
method_summary: Repeating 'hare rāma hare rāma rāma rāma hare hare, hare kṛṣṇa hare kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa hare hare'; the Kalisantaraṇa says no rule binds it, and that three and a half crore repetitions free from the gravest sins.
notes: Gauḍīya practice recites it with the 'hare kṛṣṇa' half first; the Upaniṣad gives the 'hare rāma' half first.

name: Remembering Hari as the doer; action as worship
method_summary: Doing the prescribed duties and avoiding the forbidden, without desire for results, while remembering that Hari within moves one's limbs and that all acts of mind, speech and body are his worship — the Yogadīpikā's definition of yoga.

name: Loud laughter as offering (hasita, aṭṭahāsa)
method_summary: Loud laughter ('a-ha-ha'), opening throat and lips, offered to the Lord while absorbed in meditation on Śiva.

name: Havelī kīrtan
method_summary: Temple singing of the aṣṭachāp poets' songs in classical rāgas matched to each period of the day and season, as part of the Lord's service.

name: Meditation in the heart lotus
method_summary: Seated in solitude, body straight, meditating on the Lord (with Umā; or as the thumb-sized Oṃ; or as the flame) in the heart lotus (Kaivalya 5–7; Dhyānabindu 19; Vāsudeva).

name: Meditation in the heart-lotus (Uddhava's instruction)
method_summary: Seated evenly, gaze at the nose-tip, purify the breath-channels, raise Oṃ in the heart like a bell; visualise the upturned eight-petalled heart-lotus with sun, moon and fire in its pericarp and the Lord's form in the fire; meditate on all its limbs, then on the smile, then fix the mind in space, then think of nothing; the self is seen in the Lord, light in light (BhP 11.14.32-46).

warnings.text: Keep far from the company of the attached; meditate in a secluded, safe place.

name: Closing the doors of the senses with the intellect
method_summary: With the intellect he shuts all the doors (senses), so that outwardly their working seems deranged.

name: Restraint and withdrawal of the senses
method_summary: Withdraw the senses from their objects as a tortoise draws in its limbs (2.58); restrain them first and so slay desire (3.41); move among objects with senses free of attraction and aversion (2.64); Alarka learns the senses are conquered not by force but by yoga (Anugītā 14.30).

warnings.text: The turbulent senses carry off the mind even of a wise man who strives.
Abstaining from objects removes them but not the taste, which ceases only on seeing the supreme.

name: The inner sacrifice of the senses (Anugītā)
method_summary: Contemplating the senses, mind and intellect as the seven tongues of the fire Vaiśvānara within, their objects as fuel-sticks, and the knower-functions as priests, one offers the objects into the fires within (Anugītā 14.20–24).
notes: Related to the prāṇāgnihotra of the Āraṇyakas (U02).

name: Inner worship: japa, meditation, pūjā, homa as acts of consciousness
method_summary: Outer ritual is for the gross; japa is the repeated contemplation of the supreme state, meditation the formless steady understanding, worship the firm mind in the great void, oblation the offering of elements, senses and objects with the mind into the fire of consciousness, bathing the entry into one's own nature (VBT 144-153; Paramārthasāra 74-80).

equivalents.note: inner worship (antaryāga) of other Śākta and Śaiva systems

name: Gazing on the iṣṭaliṅga (liṅga-yoga)
method_summary: Holding the liṅga on the palm at eye level and gazing on it steadily, then turning the gaze inward to the liṅga within; taught in modern Śivayoga training and associated in legend with the 'unblinking' (animiṣa) yogi.

equivalents.note: fixed gazing on an object; here the object is the worn liṅga and the practice is devotional

notes: Recorded from general knowledge of the Śivayoga revival (Hānagal Kumāra Svāmi); textual source to be found.

name: Worship of the iṣṭaliṅga on the palm
method_summary: Daily worship of one's own liṅga held on the left palm (karapīṭha) with water, ash, flowers and the like, without invocation or dismissal because Śiva already abides in it; the palm-worship is ranked above worship on an outer pedestal.

warnings.text: Never abandon liṅga-worship, even at the loss of possessions or life.

name: Devotion to Īśvara (īśvara-praṇidhāna)
method_summary: A special devotion (bhakti) to Īśvara, offering all actions to the supreme teacher or renouncing their fruit (YBh 1.23, 2.1; RM 1.23); Īśvara, won over, favours the yogin by mere intention and samādhi is near (1.23); a niyama and part of kriyā-yoga (2.1, 2.32).
signs_of_progress: realization of the inward consciousness and absence of obstacles (1.29); perfection of samādhi (2.45)

equivalents.note: Vyāsa defines praṇidhāna as a special bhakti; in Yoga its fruit is samādhi, not union with the Lord

name: Worship of the Lord (Nyāya)
method_summary: Worship (upāsti) of the Lord, declared by the wise to be the path to heaven and liberation; for the Naiyāyika it includes the reasoned contemplation of Him.

name: Offering all actions to the Lord (mad-arpaṇa)
method_summary: Whatever one does, eats, offers, gives or practises as austerity, do it as an offering to the Lord, mentally renouncing all actions in him; one is thereby freed from the bonds of action with good and evil fruits.

name: Performing dharma as an offering to the Lord (īśvarārpaṇa)
method_summary: Doing the enjoined acts with the thought of offering them to Śrī Govinda (Āpadeva) or Īśvara (Laugākṣi Bhāskara), which makes dharma a cause of the highest good; the Gītā's 'whatever you do, do it as an offering to me' is cited as authority.

name: Wrangling and cavilling to protect truth
method_summary: Using contentious debate — including quibbles and futile rejoinders, or pure refutation without a counter-thesis — only to protect an ascertained truth from opponents, as a fence of thorny branches protects seedlings.

warnings.text: Quibbles, futile rejoinders and points of defeat are defined so that they can be avoided in one's own speech and exposed in the opponent's (NBh 1.1.1); vitaṇḍā without any purpose collapses into prattle.

name: Service and worship of the jaṅgama
method_summary: Honouring, feeding and serving the wandering Śivayogins (jaṅgamas), whose sight, touch and worship sanctify, and giving them the fruits of one's work.

name: Recitation (japa)
method_summary: Repetition of sacred words: 'among sacrifices I am the sacrifice of japa' (BhG 10.25); utterance of Oṃ at death (8.13) and of 'oṃ tat sat' at the start of rites (17.23–24); the Jāpaka's recitation of the Veda/Sāvitrī in meditation without desire (MBh 12.189–193); recitation of the thousand names (13.135).

warnings.text: Recitation done with desire, pride or wrongly leads to lesser worlds, not to Brahman (as taught in the Jāpaka story).

notes: U05's contribution to a shared practice (moderate confidence on the Jāpaka details).

name: Three kinds of japa
method_summary: Loud, whispered (upāṃśu) and mental recitation, each far superior to the previous (Darśana 2; Śāṇḍilya 1.2).

name: Japa — audible, whispered, mental
method_summary: Repetition of a mantra, which surpasses ritual sacrifice tenfold when audible, a hundredfold when whispered and a thousandfold when mental; by japa alone a brāhmaṇa can reach perfection (MDh 2.85–87).

name: Braid recitation (jaṭāpāṭha)
method_summary: Reciting each pair forward, backward and forward again (ab ba ab, bc cb bc …).

name: Jātakarma (birth rite)
method_summary: At birth, before the cord is cut, the father gives the child honey and ghee, whispers 'speech' in its ear and wishes it long life and intelligence.

name: Kṛṣṇa-Jayantī fast
method_summary: Fasting on Kṛṣṇa's birthday — the dark eighth day conjoined with Rohiṇī at midnight — to be kept by all, especially the twice-born and Hari's devotees.

name: Renovation and re-consecration (jīrṇoddhāra)
method_summary: Rites for repairing a temple or replacing a damaged image, moving the deity's presence temporarily into a pot or substitute (bālālaya) and re-installing it.

name: Śrāddha for oneself while living
method_summary: A śrāddha performed for oneself during life (by those without heirs or seeking release), taught in LiP 2.45 and the Pretakalpa (ch. 8, 'self-śrāddha').
notes: Chapter titles checked (LiP 2.45 'jīvacchrāddhavidhi'; GP 2.8 'śrāddhakartr-ātmaśrāddha'); contents not read; no teaching extracted yet.

name: Combining knowledge with works
method_summary: Continuing the Vedic and social duties of one's station throughout life together with meditation on Brahman, rather than renouncing works after knowledge.

name: Breath-control as knowledge
method_summary: Exhalation as negating the world or renouncing objects, inhalation as 'I am Brahman' or scriptural knowledge, retention as steadiness in realization (Tejobindu 1.31–33; Varāha 5.58).

name: Repeated study of the science of the self
method_summary: Study and retention of the science of the self, practised constantly as study, listening and reflection.

name: Jyotiṣṭoma (the model soma sacrifice)
method_summary: The archetypal soma rite ('one desiring heaven should sacrifice with the Jyotiṣṭoma'), whose basic form is the Agniṣṭoma; Śabara names it as the paradigm of what leads to the highest good.

name: Service (kainkarya) to the Lord
method_summary: Service of the Lord in temple and home — making garlands, cleaning, cooking offerings, singing — done for his pleasure alone, the natural expression of the soul's being his servant.

name: Traditional study with the teacher (kālakṣepa)
method_summary: Study of the Śrībhāṣya, the Gītābhāṣya, the Tiruvāymoḻi commentaries and the rahasya works at the feet of a teacher of the lineage, orally, in the traditional order.

name: Skull-eating and corpse-ash practices (reported)
method_summary: Summary only: opponents report that the Kālāmukhas eat from a skull, bathe in the ash of corpses and eat it, and carry a club, as means to seen and unseen ends.

warnings.text: Yāmuna declares these acts forbidden by every scripture.

name: Pot-consecration and bathing (kalaśābhiṣeka)
method_summary: Water is consecrated in arrays of pots in which deities are invoked and then poured over the image, to renew its power or to purify after pollution (e.g. sahasrakalaśa in Kerala).

name: Kapila's eight-limbed yoga with meditation on the Lord's form
method_summary: Duty, contentment, service of self-knowers, moderate pure food, solitude, the yamas and niyamas, posture, gradual mastery of breath, withdrawal, holding breath in one of its seats with the mind, meditation on the Lord's form limb by limb, and samādhi.
signs_of_progress: melting heart, hair standing on end, the mind attaining nirvāṇa like a flame (3.28.34-35)

name: Karaṇa: bodily seals in the āṇava means
method_summary: Āṇava immersion through karaṇa - bodily postures and seals (mudrā) - one of the five āṇava supports listed in MVT 2.21 and TĀ 1.170; treated in TĀ 5 and 32.
notes: Summary only; details of the karaṇas not recorded.

name: Karma-yoga: performing one's duty without attachment to the fruit
method_summary: Perform the prescribed action (one's own dharma) as duty, with evenness in success and failure, abandoning attachment and the desire for the fruit; action so done 'for the sake of sacrifice' does not bind and purifies the self.
stage: all; for the one wishing to ascend to yoga action is the means (6.3)
prerequisites: knowledge of one's own dharma (3.35)
signs_of_progress: evenness (samatva) in success and failure; freedom from the sense of doership (5.8–9)

warnings.text: Attachment to inaction is also forbidden.
One who restrains the organs of action but dwells on objects in mind is a hypocrite.

name: Relinquishing the fruit of all actions
method_summary: Giving up the fruit of all actions, self-controlled and taking refuge in the Lord's yoga — the step for one unable even to work for the Lord (12.11), praised above meditation because peace follows immediately (12.12), and what the wise call tyāga (18.2, 18.11).

name: Karṇavedha (ear-piercing)
method_summary: Piercing the child's ears, a later addition to the lists.

name: The Kātyāyanī vow of the gopīs
method_summary: A month-long observance in Mārgaśīrṣa by unmarried girls: early bathing in the river, worship of the goddess Kātyāyanī in an image of sand, and prayer to obtain the desired husband (for the gopīs, Kṛṣṇa).

name: Kāyaka — work as worship
method_summary: Each devotee earns a living by honest work in his or her own occupation, done as worship, not interrupted even for worship, and not gathering beyond the day's need.

name: The daily round of a Kerala temple
method_summary: From the opening of the sanctum at dawn, a fixed series of pūjās through the day (dawn, morning, mid-morning, noon and night pūjās) and processional offerings (śīveli) around the shrine, performed by the śānti; the tantri intervenes for installations, festivals and purifications.
notes: Names often given: uṣaḥpūjā, etiruttu pūjā, pantīraṭi pūjā, ucca pūjā, attāḻa pūjā (from memory; unverified).

name: Keśānta / Godāna (first shave)
method_summary: The first shaving of the beard at about sixteen, with a gift of a cow.

name: Kevala-kumbhaka (retention without inhalation or exhalation)
method_summary: The spontaneous suspension of breath that arises after long practice; the Yoga Upaniṣads associate it with awakening of kuṇḍalinī and with powers. Summary only.

warnings.text: Breath must be tamed gradually, like a lion, elephant or tiger; otherwise it kills the practitioner; improper practice causes hiccup, asthma, cough and pains of head, ears and eyes.
Powers that arise must not be displayed.

name: Khecarī mudrā
method_summary: The 'moving in space' seal of the tongue, taught as a secret vidyā with a mantra (melana) received from the guru's mouth; the bodily procedures described by the texts are not reproduced. Also given inner meanings (the gaze; the renouncer's 'mudrā').

warnings.text: Learn only from a guru who knows it from text, meaning and practice; keep it secret.
Proceed gradually, never all at once, or the body perishes.

name: Singing the Lord's names (kīrtana, nāma-saṅkīrtana)
method_summary: Singing or reciting the names and deeds of the Lord, alone or together; declared the fearless way for all (BhP 2.1.11) and the means of the Kali age that gives what meditation, sacrifice and worship gave in earlier ages (BhP 12.3.51-52; VP 6.2.17).
signs_of_progress: love born, heart melted, laughing, weeping and dancing 'like one mad' (BhP 11.2.40)

warnings.text: The ten offences against the name (as cited from the Padma) obstruct its fruit.

alt_method_summary: Great souls ever sing the Lord's praise, strive, and bow to him with devotion (9.14); with minds on him they enlighten one another and always speak of him, content and rejoicing (10.9).
Gauḍīya congregational singing of the name and of Rādhā–Kṛṣṇa's play (with khol and karatāla; later padāvalī-kīrtana styles); Puṣṭimārga havelī kīrtan of the aṣṭachāp songs.
notes: U05's contribution to a shared practice.

name: Non-killing (kollāmai)
method_summary: Refraining from taking any life and protecting all creatures, even at the cost of one's own life.

name: Step recitation (kramapāṭha)
method_summary: Reciting overlapping pairs of words (ab, bc, cd …) so that both the words and their junctions are fixed; taught in the Prātiśākhyas.

warnings.text: A mantra wrong in accent or letter does not convey its meaning; as a verbal thunderbolt it harms the sacrificer, as 'Indra-śatru' did through a fault of accent.

name: Krama contemplation of the twelve Kālīs
method_summary: Contemplating every act of cognition as the sequence of the twelve Kālīs - emission, persistence, withdrawal and the nameless across object, means of knowledge and subject - until the sequence dissolves into the sequenceless (TĀ 4.148-172; Abhinavagupta's Kramastotra).

name: Feigned sleep and snoring (krāthana)
method_summary: While awake he acts as if asleep, making a snoring sound in the throat with the out-breath, so that people despise him.

warnings.text: Undertaken only after knowledge has been gained, impurity reduced and the teacher's permission obtained; the feigned acts must not conflict with the restraints (non-harming, celibacy etc.).

name: Kṛcchra penances
method_summary: Summary only: graded expiatory penances regulating food and water over a set period (Prājāpatya, Sāṃtapana, Atikṛcchra, Taptakṛcchra, Parāka) (MDh 11.211–215).

warnings.text: Penances are to be undertaken according to one's capacity and under the direction of learned authorities; the digests allow substitutes for those unable to perform them.

notes: Restricted (prolonged fasting): no quantities or durations recorded. The warning is paraphrased at chapter level (moderate).

name: Kriyā-yoga (austerity, self-study, devotion to Īśvara)
method_summary: For the unconcentrated mind: austerity, self-study and devotion to Īśvara together (2.1), to cultivate samādhi and thin the afflictions (2.2); the yogin should first be intent on it (RM 2.1).
signs_of_progress: afflictions thinned, like seeds burnt (YBh 2.2)

warnings.text: Austerity is to be practised so as not to disturb the clarity of the mind.

name: The 'razor' concentration (kṣurikā)
method_summary: A concentration that 'cuts' through the vital points and channels with mind and breath; summary only.

name: Kula worship (the 'primal sacrifice') as interpreted by Abhinavagupta
method_summary: The secret Kaula ritual of Tantrāloka 29, in which worship with a consort and the Kaula substances is presented as the outward form of the union of Śiva and Śakti in consciousness. Summary only; no procedure is given here.

warnings.text: Presented as the secret rite (rahasya) for qualified initiates only.

notes: Restricted (sexual rite).

name: Contemplation of the three targets (lakṣya-traya)
method_summary: Attending to the inner target (kuṇḍalinī, inner sound, blue light), the outer target (colours and lights in space) and the intermediate target (voids).
signs_of_progress: lights, stars, a diamond mirror, the full moon, the midday sun, a flame (Maṇḍalabrāhmaṇa 2.1)

name: The four dissolutions (Aṣṭāvakra Gītā)
method_summary: Recognizing 'I am like space, the world a pot', 'I am the ocean, the world its waves', 'I am the shell, the world the imagined silver', 'I am in all beings and they in me' — after which nothing is to be renounced, accepted or dissolved.

name: Learning from all beings (the avadhūta's method)
method_summary: Observing the ways of the elements, animals and people and drawing from each a lesson for detachment and knowledge, as the avadhūta took twenty-four teachers and his own body as a twenty-fifth.

name: Offering all enjoyment to the liṅga (arpaṇa)
method_summary: Whatever is set aside for one's own enjoyment — food, sights, sounds — is first offered to the liṅga and then received as its grace.

name: Wearing the liṅga (liṅgadhāraṇa)
method_summary: The iṣṭaliṅga, kept in a small casket (karaḍige) on a cord, is worn on the body at all times — at the head, throat, chest, armpit, belly or in the hand, never below the navel; inwardly the liṅga of light is held in the mind at the base, heart or brows.

warnings.text: Never separate the liṅga from the body at any time or place.
Wearing it below the navel is a cause of sin; not on the tip of matted hair, lower back or an unclean place.
The text treats the liṅga's accidental fall with the utmost gravity (recorded as restricted).

name: Liṅga-initiation (liṅgadīkṣā)
method_summary: The guru, with assistants, bathes the disciple with water from pots consecrated by the five brahma-mantras, whispers the five-syllable mantra secretly into the right ear, installs a purified liṅga in the disciple's life-breath and places it in his hand to be worn for life. In Liṅgāyata practice it is given to all, women and children included.
prerequisites: a qualified guru (SSM 6.1–6); the disciple's discernment and dispassion

warnings.text: The mantra is given secretly (nigūḍham).

name: Worship of the liṅga
method_summary: Worship of Śiva in the formless liṅga (including liṅgas made of earth for the occasion), with bathing, bilva leaves, lamps and offerings; the Śiva Purāṇa teaches that Śiva alone may be worshipped in the liṅga because he alone is niṣkala.

name: Burial of the dead as liṅgaikya
method_summary: The dead devotee, having become one with the liṅga, is buried seated with the liṅga in hand rather than cremated; no death-pollution or ancestral rites are observed.
notes: Community practice from general knowledge; verify the details (posture, rites) in Phase C.

name: The honey-doctrine (madhu-vidyā)
method_summary: ChU 3.1-11: meditate on the sun as the honey of the gods, the Vedas as flowers and the rays as honeycomb cells; for one who knows it the sun neither rises nor sets. BAU 2.5 (also called the madhu-brāhmaṇa): meditate on earth, waters, fire and all things as 'honey' for all beings and all beings as honey for them, culminating in 'this self is brahman'.

warnings.text: To be taught only to one's eldest son or a worthy pupil (ChU 3.11.5-6).

notes: Upaniṣadic 'vidyā' (meditation-knowledge); the Brahma Sūtra (3.3) discusses which vidyās are to be combined.

name: Bee-like alms (mādhukarī)
method_summary: The renunciant takes a little food from many houses without burdening any and stores nothing for later.
alt_method_summary: Taking a little food from several houses after the household cooking fires are out, never from a single house; eating moderately (half food, a quarter water, a quarter air).

name: Unfolding of the centre (madhyavikāsa)
method_summary: The bliss of consciousness is gained by the unfolding of the centre - the central consciousness, the suṣumnā of the breath, the gap between states - through the means listed in PH 18.

name: Mahābandha and mahāvedha
method_summary: Combined locks and the 'great piercing' named in the Yogatattva; summary only.

name: Repetition of the Mahāmṛtyuñjaya (Tryambaka) verse
method_summary: Repeating and offering with the verse 'we worship Tryambaka … may I be freed from death, not from immortality' for release from death and for health; in the Yajurveda it accompanies the Tryambaka offerings to Rudra.

name: Mahāmudrā
method_summary: The 'great seal' named among the haṭha practices of the Yogatattva and Dhyānabindu; recorded by name and purpose only.

name: The great departure (mahāprasthāna)
method_summary: Summary only: at the end of life the Pāṇḍavas renounce the kingdom and walk toward the north until the body falls (MBh 17.1–2). No instructions are given here.

warnings.text: The epic presents the departure as the close of a completed life after renunciation of kingship; each of the fallen is said to fall by his own fault, and only Yudhiṣṭhira reaches heaven in the body.
Later Dharmaśāstra authorities list the great departure among practices forbidden in the Kali age (kalivarjya).

notes: Recorded as restricted (a practice culminating in death); summary and the text's own framing only.
alt_method_summary: Summary only: a forest-hermit may set out towards the north-east, living on water and air, intent on yoga, until the body falls (MDh 6.31).
alt_notes: Restricted: recorded as the text states it; no instructions.

name: Understanding the great saying
