method_summary: Understanding 'that thou art' by first grasping the words' meanings and then, by partial implication, the consciousness common to 'that' and 'thou', with faith and the teacher's grace.

name: The great vow of the skull (mahāvrata, kapālavrata)
method_summary: Summary only: the ascetic lives as a skull-bearer - skull as begging-bowl, skull-topped staff, ash - in imitation of the Lord's penance; named 'beyond the world' for the Lākulas and the Kāpāla vow by opponents.

name: Worship and service of devotees (Māhēśvara-pūjā)
method_summary: Feeding, serving and honouring Śiva's devotees as Śiva himself; the freed soul's conduct (Civañāṉa Pōtam 12) and the practice of many Nāyaṉmārs.

name: Temple festival (mahotsava)
method_summary: The annual festival begun by hoisting the flag, with daily processions of the festival image, offerings to the attendant beings and a concluding bath (avabhṛtha/ārāṭṭu), conducted by the priest or tantri.
alt_method_summary: The annual festival: flag-hoisting, processions of the deity, and the concluding bath.

name: Reflection (manana)
method_summary: Reasoned reflection on what has been heard, removing doubts and contrary views — in Dvaita often in the company of fellow students and through the tradition's disputations.
prerequisites: śravaṇa
alt_method_summary: Continuous reasoning in harmony with the teaching to remove doubts about the object (whether the self can be Brahman), meeting objections by reasoning that does not oppose scripture.
Lineage contribution (Upaniṣadic): 'the self should be ... reflected upon (mantavya)' (BAU 2.4.5, 4.5.6).
signs_of_progress: doubt about the object (prameya-saṃśaya) removed

name: Reflection (manana) by reasoning
method_summary: Examining by reasoning, after hearing scripture, what has been heard — above all about the Lord and the self; Udayana calls such reasoning itself a form of worship.

equivalents.note: Nyāya locates itself at the manana stage of the Upaniṣadic triad; its object (a self distinct from Īśvara and from other selves) differs from Advaita's.

name: Mental temple-building and worship
method_summary: Building and consecrating a temple entirely in the mind and worshipping Śiva there, as Pūcalār and Vāyilār did.

equivalents.note: inner worship as a sustained practice rather than a ritual segment

name: Inner worship mapped onto the state beyond mind
method_summary: Each service of worship understood as a moment of the mind-less state — invocation as abandoning action, the lamp as the sun of consciousness, salutation as 'so'ham', praise as silence (Maṇḍalabrāhmaṇa 2.2).

name: Bathing in the inner tīrtha
method_summary: Cultivating truth, forbearance, sense-control, compassion, straightforwardness, giving, self-restraint, contentment, celibacy, kind speech, knowledge, steadiness and austerity - 'bathing in the lake of knowledge that removes the dirt of passion and hatred'.

name: Binding amulets (maṇi)
method_summary: Binding on an amulet of plant, wood or other substance with Atharvavedic verses for protection, health, victory or prosperity.

name: Dissolution of the mind (mano-nāśa)
method_summary: Bringing the mind to cease from forming modes, through yoga and dispassion, for the stable enjoyment of liberation while living.

name: Feigned limping (maṇṭana)
method_summary: He walks as if his foot were injured.

warnings.text: Undertaken only after knowledge has been gained, impurity reduced and the teacher's permission obtained; the feigned acts must not conflict with the restraints (non-harming, celibacy etc.).

name: The mantha rite
method_summary: A rite for one who desires greatness, performed after an observance, in which offerings of ghee are made to the breaths and other deities and a prepared mixture is drunk with formulas (BAU 6.3; ChU 5.2.4-8). Summary only.

warnings.text: It should not be taught to anyone but a son or a pupil (BAU 6.3.12).

name: Mantra repetition (the praṇava and the Viṣṇu mantras)
method_summary: Repetition of the praṇava (for renunciants, who are initiated into it) and of the eight-syllable Nārāyaṇa mantra, the twelve-syllable mantra and others derived from the praṇava, with meditation on the forms they designate.
prerequisites: dīkṣā; the praṇava for renunciants

name: Concentration on the eighteen vital points (marma)
method_summary: Holding breath and attention successively at eighteen vital points from the toes upward and back (Triśikhi 128–133; Darśana 7; Śāṇḍilya 1.69).

name: Doing the Lord's work (mat-karma)
method_summary: Be intent on doing actions for the Lord's sake — the third step of the ladder of 12.10 for one unable to practise abhyāsa; 'one who does my work... comes to me' (11.55).
stage: for those unable to practise repeated concentration (12.10)

name: Silence of the muni (mauna, mauneya)
method_summary: The state of the silent sage who, 'ecstatic with munihood', is carried by the winds while others see only his body (RV 10.136.3).
notes: The Keśin hymn describes the state, not a method.

name: Rites for retentive wisdom (medhājanana)
method_summary: Invoking Vācaspati and Medhā for the strength to retain the Veda — AVŚ 1.1 ('may Vācaspati place in me today the strengths of the thrice-seven') and 6.108 — at the start of study.

name: Moderate diet (mitāhāra)
method_summary: Sweet, unctuous food eaten leaving a quarter of the stomach empty; avoiding the hot, sour, salty, pungent; wholesome milk, ghee, wheat, mung, rice; called the chief of the yamas (Yogatattva 28–29, 46–49; Yogacūḍāmaṇi 43).

name: Moderation in food, sleep, recreation and effort
method_summary: For yoga to destroy sorrow, be moderate in food and recreation, in effort in actions, in sleep and waking (6.16–17); eat lightly in the discipline of 18.52.

warnings.text: Yoga is not for one who eats too much or not at all, sleeps too much or keeps awake too long.

name: Yoga of the Mṛgendra (seven auxiliaries)
method_summary: Breath-control (propelling, drawing in, holding), withdrawal of the mind from objects once it tastes a little ease, fixation on a chosen place, meditation as repeated thought on it, examination (ūha) of what is to be rejected and accepted, recitation bringing the object near, and absorption as unbroken flow; practised singly or together, they lead to yoga and its powers.
prerequisites: initiation; one's office as teacher or adept

warnings.text: The text itself calls the office of the initiate very hard to fulfil and requires conquest of the senses first.

notes: Breath-retention is named only; no counts or durations are recorded (restricted content policy).

name: Wearing the six insignia (reported)
method_summary: As reported by Yāmuna and Rāmānuja: knowing and wearing six insignia (ear-ornament or necklace, rucaka, earrings, crest-jewel, ash, sacred thread) with skull and khaṭvāṅga, claimed to prevent rebirth.

name: Listening to the inner sound
method_summary: The Upaniṣads mention hearing an inner sound with the ears closed: the roar or crackling of fire heard when one closes the ears is the light within (ChU 3.13.8); the sound of the digestive fire, no longer heard when one is about to depart (BAU 5.9.1); closing the ears with the thumbs one hears the sound of the space within the heart in seven forms and passes beyond it into the soundless brahman (MaiU 6.22).
signs_of_progress: the seven sounds of MaiU 6.22: like rivers, a small bell, a bronze vessel, a wheel, frogs, rain, a voice in a sheltered place
notes: Later haṭha and yoga Upaniṣads elaborate nāda practice (U28/U29).
alt_method_summary: Seated in siddhāsana, attention is held on the inner sound in the right ear; the sounds pass from loud (ocean, cloud, drum) to subtle (bells, flute, vīṇā, bee); the mind follows the subtlest until it dissolves with it.

name: Purification of the channels (nāḍī-śodhana)
method_summary: Alternate-nostril breathing in regular sessions to purify the channels, or purification by knowledge of the Self (Darśana 5). Counts and schedules given by the texts are not reproduced.
signs_of_progress: lightness, radiance, stronger digestive fire, leanness, inner sound manifest (Yogatattva 44–45; Yogacūḍāmaṇi 98–99)

warnings.text: Breath must be tamed gradually, like a lion, elephant or tiger; otherwise it kills the practitioner; improper practice causes hiccup, asthma, cough and pains of head, ears and eyes.
Breath must be tamed gradually, like a lion, elephant or tiger; otherwise it kills the practitioner; improper practice causes hiccup, asthma, cough and pains of head, ears and eyes.

name: Vedic studentship (brahmacarya), temporary or lifelong
method_summary: Living in the teacher's house after initiation: begging, bringing fuel, tending the fire, serving the teacher, chastity and study; the lifelong (naiṣṭhika) student serves the teacher until death (MDh 2; ŚB 11.3.3).
duration: 12 years per Veda or until mastered; or lifelong

name: Repetition of the divine name on beads (nāma-japa)
method_summary: Softly repeating the names of Kṛṣṇa (in Gauḍīya practice, above all the Hare Kṛṣṇa mahāmantra) on a string of tulasī beads, attentively and free of the ten offences; Haridāsa Ṭhākura's daily vow of three hundred thousand names is the model; later institutions fix a daily minimum (e.g. ISKCON's sixteen rounds, recent). In the Puṣṭimārga the refuge mantra 'śrī kṛṣṇaḥ śaraṇaṃ mama' is repeated.
signs_of_progress: taste for the name (ruci)
tears, faltering voice, horripilation while chanting (Śikṣāṣṭaka 6)

warnings.text: Chanting while committing the ten offences does not yield love; sinning on the strength of the name is itself an offence.

equivalents.note: general mantra repetition; here the object is the name itself, held non-different from Kṛṣṇa

name: Congregational chanting of the name (nāma-saṅkīrtana)
method_summary: Singing the Lord's names together, aloud, with drums (khol/mṛdaṅga) and cymbals, in homes, temples and street processions (nagara-saṅkīrtana), led by a lead singer with response; held to be the dharma of Kali and the most potent limb; to be done with humility (Śikṣāṣṭaka 3).
signs_of_progress: dancing and ecstatic signs
humility and tolerance

equivalents.note: the Purāṇic kīrtana; Gauḍīya saṅkīrtana is congregational and name-centred

name: Nāmakaraṇa (naming)
method_summary: Naming the child on the tenth or twelfth day, with names auspicious and suited to the class.

name: Prostration as offering (namaskāra)
method_summary: Homage to the Lord within the offering, performed mentally according to the Ratnaṭīkā; self-offering is made with prostrations while repeating the five mantras.

name: Recitation of the eight-syllable Nārāyaṇa mantra
method_summary: Recitation of 'oṃ namo nārāyaṇāya', which leads to Vaikuṇṭha and is the tāraka (Nārāyaṇa; Tārasāra; Ātmabodha).

name: Nārāyaṇa-bali
method_summary: An offering to Nārāyaṇa for one who died a bad or untimely death, allowing the regular rites to take effect.

name: Gazing toward the tip of the nose (nāsikāgra-dṛṣṭi)
method_summary: While seated erect for meditation, direct the gaze toward the tip of one's own nose without looking about in any direction.
notes: Śaṅkara glosses: as if gazing at the tip of the nose, i.e. with the gaze turned inward, not literally fixed on it; U05's contribution to a practice also covered by the haṭha units.

name: The nine forms of devotion (navadhā bhakti)
method_summary: Devotion practised as hearing, singing and remembering the Lord's names and deeds, serving his feet, ritual worship, obeisance, servitude, friendship and complete self-offering, performed directly toward the Lord (BhP 7.5.23-24); the Śiva Purāṇa gives Śaivas the three means of hearing, singing and reflection.
signs_of_progress: melting of the heart, tears, laughter, song and dance (BhP 11.14.24; 11.2.40)

warnings.text: One who seeks blessings in return is a merchant, not a servant.

name: The nine means of devotion (Adhyātma Rāmāyaṇa)
method_summary: Practising the nine means taught to Śabarī, beginning with holy company and ending with inquiry into the Lord's nature.

name: The Navarātra vow of the Goddess
method_summary: Nine nights of worship of the Goddess (especially in autumn), with recitation of the Devī Māhātmya and worship of young girls.

name: Negation 'not this, not this'
method_summary: In the Rāma Gītā: negating the whole world by 'not this', tasting the consciousness in the heart and setting the world aside like the rind of a fruit whose juice is drunk.
notes: U06 contribution to a shared practice id (principal source: Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad).
alt_method_summary: Lineage contribution (Upaniṣadic): the self or brahman is indicated by the instruction 'not so, not so', denying of it every graspable form — it is ungraspable, indestructible, unattached, unbound (BAU 2.3.6, 3.9.26, 4.2.4, 4.4.22, 4.5.15); the text states it as an instruction (ādeśa), not as a graded exercise.

Negating every object, attribute and adjunct as not the self ('I am not the body, senses, mind…'), until only the undeniable witnessing consciousness remains; the negation is of specifications, not of Brahman.
Sāṃkhya contribution: discrimination is accomplished through practice of the principles by giving up each with 'not this, not this' (SS 3.76).

name: Meditation (nididhyāsana / dhyāna)
method_summary: Sustained meditation on the Lord. In Dvaita: meditation on Viṣṇu with the qualities suited to one's fitness, within one's heart as the original (bimba) of one's self; it is an independent means (not a subsidiary of hearing) and yields the direct realization that pleases the Lord.
prerequisites: śravaṇa
manana
bhakti
signs_of_progress: direct realization (aparokṣa) of the Lord, within the scope one's fitness allows
contrary notions (viparīta-bhāvanā) weaken
savikalpa then nirvikalpa samādhi

warnings.text: One who strives for a vision he is unfit for falls even from what he had.

alt_method_summary: A continuous flow of the thought of the self as Brahman, excluding contrary ideas, to remove the deep-rooted habit of identifying with body and mind; culminates in (savikalpa and nirvikalpa) samādhi; for the Bhāmatī the principal means, making mediate knowledge direct.
Lineage contribution (Upaniṣadic): 'the self should be ... meditated upon (nididhyāsitavya)'; by seeing, hearing, reflecting on and understanding the self all this is known (BAU 2.4.5, 4.5.6).

name: Attributeless devotion
method_summary: Letting the mind flow to the Lord at the mere hearing of his qualities, without motive or interruption, desiring nothing, not even liberation, apart from his service.

name: Meditation on the attributeless (nirguṇa-upāsanā)
method_summary: For those unable to inquire: meditating on the attributeless Brahman as 'I am Brahman', which, like following a gem's light, leads to knowledge; also separating being–shining–dear from name and form in all things.

name: Wearing the used garland (nirmālya)
method_summary: He wears flowers taken down from the image, to increase devotion and show the sign.

name: Liberating initiation (nirvāṇa-dīkṣā)
method_summary: The guru ritually traverses and purifies the six paths of the disciple's bondage, burning accumulated and future karma, leaving only the karma that sustains the present body; the disciple becomes a putraka assured of liberation at death. Summary only.
prerequisites: samaya-dīkṣā
alt_method_summary: The liberating initiation: the guru purifies the six paths in the disciple and burns the bonds; with 'seed' the initiate keeps the post-initiatory rules, 'seedless' for those unable to; liberation follows at the fall of the body.

name: Nirvikalpa samādhi (Vedānta)
method_summary: Absorption in which the mode in the form of Brahman remains without distinction of knower and known, like salt dissolved in water; its eight auxiliaries are the yoga limbs and its obstacles dullness, distraction, latent attachment and relishing.

warnings.text: Four obstacles: laya, vikṣepa, kaṣāya, rasāsvāda.

name: Meditation as objectless mind (dhyāna)
method_summary: Meditation is the removal of passion, accomplished through the cessation of the mind's modifications; meditation is mind without object; supported by concentration, posture, one's own duty, dispassion and practice, turning away from torpor and distraction, in any place where the mind is serene.
prerequisites: dispassion, practice, one's own duty (SS 3.32–36)
signs_of_progress: coloring of puruṣa calmed, puruṣa abiding in itself like a crystal (SS 2.34–35)

warnings.text: Torpor and distraction are to be turned away from.

name: Niṣkramaṇa (first outing)
method_summary: Taking the child out to see the sun in the fourth month.

name: Performing obligatory and occasional rites while abstaining from desire-prompted and prohibited acts
method_summary: The discipline of the one seeking release: continue the obligatory and occasional rites to avoid the demerit of omission (and, for Kumārila, to destroy past sin), abstain from desire-prompted acts that would produce new bodies and from prohibited acts; past karma is exhausted by experience.
prerequisites: eligibility for Vedic rites; aversion to saṃsāra (Śāstradīpikā, Prakaraṇapañcikā)
signs_of_progress: (not described in the sources checked)

name: Performance of obligatory duties for purification
method_summary: Performing the daily and occasional rites and one's duties without desire for their fruits, offered to the Lord, avoiding desire-prompted and forbidden acts, for the purification of mind that makes one fit for knowledge.

name: Discrimination of the eternal and the non-eternal
method_summary: Cultivating the firm conviction that Brahman alone is eternal and real and all else transient; the first of the four qualifications.

name: Ever-arisen samādhi (nityodita-samādhi)
method_summary: In the emergence from samādhi, while its impressions remain, reflecting again and again on oneness with consciousness until samādhi is continuous in all activity (PH 19); Kṣemarāja calls this state the kramamudrā.

name: The observances (niyama)
method_summary: Purity, contentment, austerity, self-study and devotion to Īśvara (2.32, YBh 2.32).
signs_of_progress: the fruits of 2.40–45

name: Recitation of the Narasiṃha mantra-king
method_summary: The anuṣṭubh 'king of mantras' of Narasiṃha, by which Prajāpati creates (Nṛsiṃhapūrvatāpanī; Avyakta).

name: Dance as offering (nṛtta)
method_summary: Dance with gestures of hands and feet according to the Nāṭyaśāstra, offered together with song.

name: Placing letters and syllables on the body (nyāsa)
method_summary: In the Devī Gītā's daily worship: placing the letters (mātṛkā-nyāsa) and the syllable hrīṃ (hṛllekhā) in the body.
notes: U06 contribution to a shared practice id.
alt_method_summary: The worshipper touches or visualises parts of the body while installing mantras — letters of the alphabet (mātṛkā), the limb-mantras, the five brahma-mantras or the deity's mantras — making the body a divine mantra-body fit to worship the deity; the same is done on the image.
Installing the brahma- and limb-mantras on the hands and body so that the worshipper becomes Śiva for the worship.

name: Yoga and the practice of samādhi (Nyāya)
method_summary: Repeated practice of a particular samādhi as the means to knowledge of truth, in solitary places such as forests, caves and sandbanks, with the method of the inner self learned from the Yoga śāstra — austerity, breath-control, sense-withdrawal, meditation and fixation — and repeated contemplation of sense-objects to abandon attachment and aversion.
stage: after purification by yama and niyama

warnings.text: Objects intrude by their force and hunger and the like drive one away from samādhi; its arising depends on the continuing effect of previous practice.

equivalents.note: Vātsyāyana refers the method to the Yoga śāstra and names limbs of it; Nyāya's aim is knowledge of the self as distinct, not the Yoga's isolation of puruṣa.

name: Meditation on Oṃ (MkP 42)
method_summary: Repeat and contemplate the one syllable Oṃ: its three measures (a, u, m) and the half-measure beyond the guṇas felt at the crown; breath the bow, self the arrow, Brahman the target; become one with the imperishable.

name: Meditation on Oṃ with fixation in the heart
method_summary: Self-controlled, after reciting the chosen Gāyatrī, he meditates on the syllable Oṃ and holds the mind fixed in the heart.

name: Word-by-word recitation (padapāṭha)
method_summary: Reciting the Saṃhitā word by word, with sandhi undone and compound members marked, as fixed in the Padapāṭha ascribed to Śākalya.

warnings.text: A mantra wrong in accent or letter does not convey its meaning; as a verbal thunderbolt it harms the sacrificer, as 'Indra-śatru' did through a fault of accent.

name: Receiving pādōdaka
method_summary: Receiving as sacrament the water in which the feet of the guru or jaṅgama have been washed; one of the eight shields.

name: Discrimination of the five sheaths (pañca-kośa-viveka)
method_summary: Examining each sheath in turn — food, vital air, mind, intellect, bliss — as changing and known, hence not the self, until the self as their witness and support is recognized.

name: The five great daily sacrifices
method_summary: Each day the householder studies/teaches the Veda (to Brahman), offers water to the ancestors, an oblation into fire to the gods, food-offerings (bali) to beings and hospitality to guests (to men) (ŚB 11.5.6.1–3; TA 2.10; MDh 3.68–70).

name: Muttering the five brahma-mantras
method_summary: Muttering of the Sadyojāta, Vāmadeva, Aghora, Tatpuruṣa and Īśāna mantras (the five purifiers) during the ash-bath, the offering and circumambulation; muttering the five alone is also a cause of merit.

name: Observance of the five codes (pañcācāra)
method_summary: Living by liṅgācāra, sadācāra, śivācāra, bhṛtyācāra and gaṇācāra: exclusive worship of the liṅga, honest life, equality of devotees, humility and defence of the community.

name: Meditation on the five fires (pañcāgni-vidyā)
method_summary: Know yonder world, the rain-god, this world, man and woman as five sacrificial fires into which faith, Soma, rain, food and semen are offered; knowing this (with faith and austerity) one goes by the path of the gods and is not stained even by association with those who fall.
notes: Upaniṣadic 'vidyā' (meditation-knowledge); the Brahma Sūtra (3.3) discusses which vidyās are to be combined.

name: The five daily periods (pañcakāla)
method_summary: The Pāñcarātrin's day is divided into approach (abhigamana: purification and going to the Lord), gathering (upādāna: collecting materials for worship), worship (ijyā), study (svādhyāya) and meditation (yoga).
notes: The five also appear, as the Bhāgavatas' practice, in Śaṅkara's report.
alt_method_summary: The day divided into five periods: approach (abhigamana), gathering materials (upādāna), worship (ijyā), study (svādhyāya) and meditation (yoga), as practised by Śrīvaiṣṇavas following the Pāñcarātra and the Nityagrantha.

name: Repetition of the five-syllable mantra
method_summary: Repetition of 'namaḥ śivāya' (six-syllabled with Oṃ) received at initiation, spoken, whispered or — best — mentally, after three breath-restraints, facing east or north and contemplating Śiva in the heart; also used in worshipping the liṅga.

warnings.text: Vows of living on water or air and other emaciating austerities do not reach Śiva's world.

alt_method_summary: Repeating and meditating na-ma-śi-vā-ya (or śivāya namaḥ) — aloud, softly or mentally — as refuge and as the means of purification; Tamil Siddhānta teaches the letters' meaning so that the soul turns toward grace.
Repetition of 'namaḥ śivāya' (with Oṃ, six syllables), received from the teacher, as the chief means of Śaiva worship and liberation.
prerequisites: in Siddhānta teaching, received from the guru

name: The five sacraments (pañcasaṃskāra, samāśrayaṇa)
method_summary: Śrīvaiṣṇava initiation by the teacher: the marks of discus and conch on the shoulders (tāpa), the upright forehead mark (puṇḍra), a servant-name (nāma), the three secret mantras (mantra) and instruction in worship (yāga). Summary only.
notes: U14's contribution to U08's entry; Rāmānuja received it from Periya Nambi at Madhurāntakam.
alt_method_summary: Initiation of a Vaiṣṇava by branding with the discus and conch (tāpa), the sectarian mark (puṇḍra), a new name (nāma), the mantra, and instruction in worship (yāga). Summary only.
alt_notes: Vaikhānasas do not take the branding (see cpt:garbha-vaisnava).

name: Worship of the five deities (pañcāyatana-pūjā)
method_summary: Domestic worship of Śiva, Viṣṇu, Devī, Sūrya and Gaṇeśa (one at the centre as the chosen deity), which the Smārta tradition credits Śaṅkara with systematizing; worship of the qualified Brahman for purification and devotion.
notes: Tradition's account; the attribution to Śaṅkara is not supported by his accepted works.

name: Temple worship for others (parārtha-pūjā)
method_summary: Public worship in temples with installed liṅgas or images, performed by qualified priests on behalf of the king, the realm and devotees; its rules are the subject of most South Indian Āgama redactions.
alt_method_summary: Worship performed for others in the temple by consecrated Ādiśaiva priests.

name: Parisaṃkhyāna meditation (Upadeśasāhasrī)
method_summary: Reviewing each object of the senses as not-self and changing and oneself as pure, unrelated, changeless awareness, so as to cease identifying with them and to stop generating merit and demerit.

name: Wandering (pārivrājya) and the rains retreat
method_summary: Wandering alone or with one companion; one night in a village, five in a town, seven at a sacred place; staying in one place during the four rainy months; dwelling in empty houses, temples, tree-roots, caves.

name: Pariyaṅka yōkam
method_summary: A yoga of the third tantra of the Tirumantiram involving union with a consort; recorded as a name and summary only.

warnings.text: Restricted practice: no method recorded. The text places it within guru-directed yoga (specific warnings not verified).

name: The Uḍupi paryāya of Kṛṣṇa worship
method_summary: The worship of the Kṛṣṇa image installed by Madhva at Uḍupi, performed in rotation by the heads of the eight maṭhas, each holding the turn (paryāya) for two years.
notes: The rotation rules are recorded from memory (see lin:udupi-asta-matha).

name: The animal sacrifice (paśubandha)
method_summary: The offering of an animal bound to the sacrificial post (yūpa); recorded as a summary only.

warnings.text: The Vedic verses ask that the victim 'not die but go to the gods by easy paths'; later traditions (Upaniṣadic, Jain, Buddhist, Vaiṣṇava) criticize or replace animal offerings.

name: Pāśupata initiation
method_summary: The teacher tests a brahmin, consecrates him in the forenoon before the southern image of Mahādeva with ash sanctified by the five mantras, and makes him hear the mantra; material, time, rite, image and teacher are the five factors.
prerequisites: brahmin male, tested by the teacher; freedom from debts (Kuśika's declaration)

name: The six-limbed offering (upahāra)
method_summary: Kneeling south of the image after the ash-bath, the practitioner mutters, then laughs loudly again and again, sings and dances, makes the bull-like ḍuṇḍuṅ sound, prostrates and mutters, then reports the offering to the Lord, circumambulates and takes a closing bath.

warnings.text: Where worldly people are present, all this is to be done secretly.

notes: The Ratnaṭīkā classes muttering and prostration as mental, dance as bodily, and laughter, song and the ḍuṇḍuṅ sound as vocal.

name: The pāśupata vow
method_summary: Taking ash with 'fire is ash, wind is ash…' and smearing the body, for release of the paśu from its bonds (Atharvaśiras 5).

name: The Pāśupata livelihoods
method_summary: Alms (first and third stages), discarded food (second), whatever comes (fourth); in the fifth there is none. Alms are gathered with purity, avoiding certain houses, and offered to Śiva before eating; he lives after the manner of cows and deer and is purified by water alone.

name: Pāśupata yoga of the Īśvara Gītā
method_summary: Taking ash from the sacred fire and smearing all the limbs while reciting the 'agnir iti' mantras, then meditating on Īśāna, the supreme light, within; for celibate twice-born devotees.
prerequisites: devotion to Śiva
celibacy (brahmacarya)

name: Offering a leaf, flower, fruit or water with devotion
method_summary: Offer to the Lord with devotion even a leaf, a flower, a fruit or water; he accepts the loving offering of the pure-hearted (9.26).

name: Annual pavitra offering (pavitrārohaṇa)
method_summary: In Śrāvaṇa (or Nabhasya) the worshipper offers a consecrated thread-garland (pavitra) to the deity to make good all defects in the year's worship and complete the annual observance.

name: Offering piṇḍas for the dead
method_summary: Offering rice-balls with sesame and water to the dead for the first ten days (which build the preta's body), then monthly through the year.

name: Offering to the fathers (piṇḍapitṛyajña)
method_summary: Offering rice-balls and water to the three generations of fathers, who are called to come with svadhā.
alt_method_summary: The Śrauta new-moon offering of rice-balls to the three nearest ancestors, performed with the sacred cord over the right shoulder, since the fathers receive food monthly (ŚB 2.4.2).

name: Vedic funeral (pitṛmedha / antyeṣṭi as the hymns give it)
method_summary: Cremation or burial with the funeral hymns: the corpse on the pyre is sent to the fathers with Agni asked to carry, not consume, it; the flesh-eating fire is sent away; the widow rises from beside the dead; the living set a boundary against death; the bones are laid in the earth; the fathers are invited to the offerings.

equivalents.note: The Saṃhitā hymns supply the mantras of the later gṛhya funeral (antyeṣṭi); the procedures are fixed in the sūtras.

name: Expulsion and retention of breath (1.34)
method_summary: Steadying the mind by expelling the air of the abdomen through the nostrils with a special effort and by holding it (1.34, YBh 1.34). Summary only.
notes: No measures are given in the YS; haṭha texts add warnings about breath practice (units U28/U29).

name: Circumambulation (pradakṣiṇa)
method_summary: Clockwise circling of the image while muttering, after the offering; one of the vows. The Sūtra adds that in Rudra's worship the counter-clockwise too is clockwise.

name: Breath as sacrifice: offering prāṇa and apāna
method_summary: As a form of sacrifice, some offer the in-breath into the out-breath and the out-breath into the in-breath, restraining their movement (4.29); in meditation the two breaths moving in the nostrils are made equal (5.27). The Gītā gives no counts or durations.
notes: Summary only; the Gītā prescribes no retention measures.

name: Bhuśuṇḍa's contemplation of the breath
method_summary: Continuous contemplation of the natural movement of prāṇa and apāna from and to the heart, attending to the points where each subsides and resting in the Self in the pauses between them.
notes: Summary only; no counts or durations are recorded. The YV presents it as akin to contemplation of the Self, not as forced retention.

name: Stilling mind through the breath (Yoga Vāsiṣṭha)
method_summary: Because the vibration of prāṇa is one seed of the mind, yogins calm the mind by restraining the breath through prāṇāyāma, meditation and skilful methods; the other seed, vāsanā, must also be given up.

warnings.text: The Yoga Vāsiṣṭha holds that breath-stilling alone is insufficient without giving up vāsanās and gaining knowledge (U06 summary of 5.92).

name: Meditation on breath as brahman
method_summary: Venerate breath as the eldest and best, as brahman (KauU 2.1-2; ChU 4.10.4), as life and immortality (KauU 3.2); know its food and clothing (BAU 6.1.14; ChU 5.2).

name: Prāṇāgnihotra (offering food into the breaths)
method_summary: At each meal the eater sips water ('immortal under-layer'), offers the first five morsels with 'svāhā' to prāṇa, apāna, vyāna, udāna and samāna, meditating that each breath, sense, deity and region is satisfied, and ends with water ('immortal covering'); eating is thus an Agnihotra offered in the self (ChU 5.19–24; TA 10.69–70).
signs_of_progress: 'his evils are burned up like a reed-tuft in fire' (ChU 5.24.3)

warnings.text: Offered without knowing its meaning, the Agnihotra is 'like pouring the offering on ashes' (ChU 5.24.1).

alt_method_summary: The first morsels of each meal are offered with 'to prāṇa svāhā', then to vyāna, apāna, samāna and udāna; each offering satisfies the corresponding sense, deity and world; done with knowledge it is an agnihotra into the vaiśvānara self that burns up all evils.
Before eating, food is sprinkled with mantras and offered in five oblations to the five breaths; the body is the sacrificial ground.

name: Contemplation of the inner liṅga of light
method_summary: Continuous contemplation of the jyotirliṅga at the base, in the heart or between the brows — gold, coral-red and crystal respectively — and setting the breath in the liṅga and the liṅga in the breath with a still mind.
signs_of_progress: loss of taste for the outer (SSM 6.44)
the liṅga shines within like a lamp (SSM 12.8)

name: Meditation on Oṃ (praṇava)
method_summary: Contemplation and repetition of Oṃ through its measures to the half-measure and the soundless; Oṃ as bow, chariot or fire-stick; also joined with breath-regulation.
signs_of_progress: Brahman shines within twelve months for one who repeats 12,000 praṇavas daily (Sannyāsa 2.103–104)

name: Repetition of Oṃ with contemplation of Īśvara (praṇava-japa)
method_summary: Repeating the praṇava, Īśvara's designator, while contemplating its meaning, Īśvara (1.27–28, YBh 1.28); alternating self-study and yoga ('from self-study to yoga, from yoga to self-study').
signs_of_progress: one-pointed mind (YBh 1.28); inward consciousness realized, obstacles absent (1.29)

name: Dissolving the syllables of Oṃ into the Self (Rāma Gītā)
method_summary: Before samādhi, contemplating the world as Oṃ; dissolving A (the waking viśva) into U, U (the dreaming taijasa) into M, and M (the sleeping prājña) into the Self, dense consciousness: 'I am the supreme Brahman'.

name: Breath purification with Oṃ (Uddhava Gītā)
method_summary: Purifying the breath's path by inhalation, retention and exhalation and their reverse, raising the unbroken Oṃ from the heart like a bell's sound; the text gives it as done ten times at each of the three junctions of the day, mastering the breath within a month.

name: Meditation on Om (praṇava-upāsanā)
method_summary: Meditate on the self as Om; Om is the bow, the self the arrow, brahman the target, to be pierced by one who is undistracted (MuU 2.2.3-6); the body as lower fire-stick and Om as upper, by the friction of meditation one sees God (ŚU 1.14); meditating on Om with one, two or three measures until death leads to the human world, the moon or the brahma-world (PrU 5); A, U, M and the measureless correspond to the four quarters (MāU); Om as the best support (KU 1.2.15-17).

equivalents.note: Purāṇic meditation on Om (U07)
Yoga Sūtra 1.27-28 repetition of Om (U10); the Upaniṣads speak of meditation (upāsanā, abhidhyāna) rather than repetition

alt_method_summary: Fixing the mind on Oṃ, whose sounds a, u, m correspond to waking, dream and sleep and whose soundless 'fourth' to turīya; Oṃ is the fearless Brahman.

name: Breath-regulation (prāṇāyāma)
method_summary: With posture mastered, cutting off the movement of inhalation and exhalation (2.49): external, internal or suspended, observed by place, time and number, becoming long and subtle (2.50, YBh 2.50). Summary only; no measures or counts.
prerequisites: mastery of posture (2.49)
signs_of_progress: the covering of the light dwindles (2.52); the mind becomes fit for concentration (2.53)
notes: YBh 2.52 quotes: 'There is no austerity higher than prāṇāyāma.' Haṭha texts add warnings (U28/U29).
alt_method_summary: Lineage contribution (Upaniṣadic): first limb of the Maitrī's yoga (6.18); ŚU 2.9: restraining the breaths with movements controlled, breathe out through the nose when the breath is diminished.
Sāṃkhya contribution: restraint (of breath) by expulsion and retention, as a support of meditation (SS 3.33); no further detail is given in the sūtra.

warnings.text: Breath is let out gently, through the nose (ŚU 2.9).

name: Purāṇic prāṇāyāma
method_summary: Breath-mastery in exhalation, inhalation and retention, neither hurried nor slow, after purifying the channels, practised gradually and often joined with mantra (with 'seed') or without; it burns faults and brings calm, the dispelling of darkness, inner light and clarity.
notes: Summary only: the texts' counts and grades of retention are not reproduced.

warnings.text: Practise neither fast nor slow, step by step.
Do not practise overfed, hungry, tired or in unsuitable places and times; faults such as deafness, dullness and fever follow.

name: Approaching the teacher: prostration, inquiry and service
method_summary: Learn knowledge from those who have seen the truth by prostrating before them, questioning them and serving them (4.34); service of the teacher (ācāryopāsana) is among the marks of knowledge (13.7).

name: Surrender (prapatti / śaraṇāgati)
method_summary: Taking refuge in the Lord alone: resolving to do what pleases him, rejecting what displeases him, trusting his protection, choosing him as protector, offering oneself and living in humility.

name: Surrender (prapatti / śaraṇāgati) in the Śrīvaiṣṇava tradition
method_summary: Taking refuge, once and for all, at the feet of Nārāyaṇa with Śrī as the sole means, through a teacher, typically by reciting the dvaya: with resolve to please, avoidance of displeasing, great faith, choosing him as protector, helplessness, and laying down the burden of one's protection; thereafter living in service, free from anxiety about salvation. The Vaṭakalai treat it as a means performed; the Teṅkalai as acceptance of the Lord as the means.
stage: open to all, of any class or gender
prerequisites: ākiñcanya and ananyagatitva
initiation by a teacher (pañcasaṃskāra)
knowledge of the artha-pañcaka
signs_of_progress: freedom from anxiety (the Lord's 'do not grieve')
desire for service only

equivalents.note: the same six-limbed surrender of the Pāñcarātra (U08)

warnings.text: To regard one's own surrender as the means is a fault (Teṅkalai).
Surrender must not be repeated as a means; repetition is allowed only as expiation (Vaṭakalai).

name: Receiving prasāda
method_summary: Eating only what has first been offered to the liṅga, and receiving the prasāda of guru and jaṅgama, for purity of mind.

name: Prasaṅkhyāna (repeated contemplation after verbal knowledge)
method_summary: In Maṇḍana's view, repeatedly contemplating the knowledge obtained from the Upaniṣads until it becomes direct and destroys the impressions of difference; regarded as unnecessary for the fully qualified by Śaṅkara (US 18) and Sureśvara.

name: Repeated contemplation of objects and of the body (prasaṅkhyāna)
method_summary: First contemplating the objects of desire whose false construction breeds attachment, aversion and delusion, until that false construction ceases; then contemplating the body and the rest within, until the I-notion ceases; one who dwells detached within and without is called liberated.
signs_of_progress: false construction ceases
I-notion ceases
mind detached within and without

name: Pratardana's inner Agnihotra (saṃyamana)
method_summary: Knowing that while speaking one offers breath into speech and while breathing offers speech into breath, one treats these as two endless oblations offered continuously, waking and sleeping (KU 2.5 = ŚĀ 4.5).

name: Pratardana's meditation on breath as the intelligent self
method_summary: Venerate Indra/breath as the intelligent self (prajñātman), as life and immortality; know not speech but the speaker, not the object but the knower.
notes: Brahma Sūtra 1.1.28-31 discusses this passage. Upaniṣadic 'vidyā' (meditation-knowledge); the Brahma Sūtra (3.3) discusses which vidyās are to be combined.

name: Cultivating the opposite (pratipakṣa-bhāvanā)
method_summary: When harmful thoughts arise, reflect on their opposites: that violence and the rest, done, caused or approved, from greed, anger or delusion, mild to intense, bear endless suffering and ignorance; that having taken refuge in yoga by granting fearlessness to all beings, to take such thoughts up again is to be like a dog eating its vomit (2.33–34, YBh 2.33–34).

warnings.text: Harmful thoughts have endless suffering and ignorance as their fruit.

name: Installation and consecration (pratiṣṭhā)
method_summary: The series of rites that establish the deity in a liṅga or image and its temple: preparatory rites on the image, its immersion and rest, installation on the pedestal, infusion of the deity through mantras, and the first worship; to be performed throughout with a single root scripture (Śaiva rule), by the tantri alone (Kerala).

warnings.text: Installation done with a sub-division (upabheda) instead of a root āgama destroys the performer and the patron.

name: Recognition (pratyabhijñā) of one's self as the Lord
method_summary: Recognizing, through the revealed powers of knowing and acting present in every experience, that one's own self is Maheśvara; established once with firm conviction, recognition itself is liberation; the mind turned inward ascends to consciousness (ĪPK 1.1.3, 4.16-17; PH 13).
signs_of_progress: bliss of consciousness; lordship persisting amid thought (ĪPK 4.12)

name: Sense-withdrawal (pratyāhāra)
method_summary: The senses, disjoined from their objects, follow the stilled mind as bees follow the queen bee (2.54, YBh 2.54).
signs_of_progress: supreme mastery of the senses (2.55)
alt_method_summary: Lineage contribution (Upaniṣadic): second limb in MaiU 6.18; draw the senses with the mind into the heart (ŚU 2.8); turn the sight inward (KU 2.1.1); draw all the senses into the self (ChU 8.15.1).

name: Pravargya (the hot-milk rite)
method_summary: A rite within the Soma sacrifice in which milk is heated in a clay pot (mahāvīra) until it glows; explained as restoring the head of the sacrifice cut off from Makha/Viṣṇu (ŚB 14.1–3; TA 4–5); secret, taught apart.

warnings.text: Treated as a dangerous, secret rite to be learned apart (in the Āraṇyaka) from a qualified teacher.

alt_method_summary: The secret rite of the heated pot (gharma) of milk, taught in the forest; its mantras stand in the last books of the Vājasaneyi Saṃhitā and in the Āraṇyakas.

name: Expiatory rites (prāyaścitta)
method_summary: Rites that make good lapses in worship, breaches of observance and pollutions of the temple, graded by the gravity of the fault.
alt_method_summary: Occasional rites enjoined on the occasion of a fault, omission or mishap in performance (treated in MS 6.4 and elsewhere).

name: Expiation by confession, remorse, austerity and recitation
method_summary: The sinner declares his deed, repents, resolves not to repeat it, performs austerity and Vedic recitation (and gives gifts in distress); as the mind condemns the deed, so the body is freed from it (MDh 11.227–232).

name: The prayer of the dying (Īśa 15-18)
method_summary: At death one asks Pūṣan to uncover the face of truth covered by the golden vessel, affirms 'that person yonder, I am he', commits breath to the wind and body to ashes, bids the mind remember what was done, and asks Agni to lead by the good path (Īśa 15-18; BAU 5.15).

name: Fasting unto death (prāyopaveśa)
method_summary: The vow of sitting without food until death with the mind fixed on the Lord, as Parīkṣit did on the Gaṅgā after the curse. Recorded only as the text's narrative.
notes: Restricted (prolonged fasting): summary only. The Pretakalpa has a chapter on the destiny of those who die by fasting (2.36, title checked, content not read).

name: Going about like a wretch (pretācaraṇa)
method_summary: He lives unwashed, dirt-smeared, with hair, beard and nails grown and without grooming, like a poor madman, so that the marks of caste and āśrama are cut off and dispassion grows.

name: Ritual worship of the deity (pūjā, arcana)
method_summary: Worship of the deity in an image, liṅga or yantra with offerings; one of the nine forms of devotion and the chief means of the Dvāpara age.
alt_method_summary: After bathing and the purifications of self, place, substances, mantras and support, the worshipper purifies the elements of the body, installs mantras on the body (nyāsa), worships the deity inwardly and then outwardly in liṅga, image, maṇḍala or fire with offerings (water, flowers, incense, lamp, food), recitation and praise, and concludes with fire offering and dismissal. Śaiva texts distinguish worship for oneself and for others; the Pāñcarātrin performs it as the third of five daily periods; Vaikhānasas worship the movable image fully and the fixed image with flowers; in Kerala the śānti performs a fixed sequence of daily pūjās.

Gauḍīya deity worship (arcana, śrī-mūrti-sevā) according to the Haribhaktivilāsa, with offerings, ārati and prasāda; serving the deity with faith is one of the five most potent limbs. Puṣṭimārga service of the Lord's form (sevā) in the havelī follows the eight daily periods.

name: Abstaining from meat (pulāl maṟuttal)
method_summary: Refusing flesh food, praised above a thousand sacrifices.

name: Puṃsavana (rite for a male child)
method_summary: A rite in the third month of pregnancy, before the embryo 'moves', for a male child.

name: Hearing the Purāṇa (kathā-śravaṇa)
method_summary: Listening with faith to the recitation and exposition of the Purāṇa by a qualified reciter, the first step of the Bhāgavata's path (hearing leads to taste, purification, steady devotion and knowledge of the Lord), with rules for giving and honouring the text.

name: Preparatory mantra practice (puraścaraṇa)
method_summary: Before a mantra is used for rites, the practitioner masters it by a prescribed course of repetition with fire offering and other supplements, under dietary and conduct rules. Summary only.
notes: U31 owns mantra practice; no counts recorded here.

name: Pure food taken with restraint
method_summary: Eating food that is pure — of desirable colour, taste, smell and touch, sprinkled and consecrated, given by the untainted and taken with the proper recitation — together with self-restraint, since without restraint pure food yields no prosperity; taint lies in injury.

name: The meditation on the person as sacrifice (puruṣa-vidyā)
method_summary: Regard one's life as a soma sacrifice: the first twenty-four years as the morning pressing, the next forty-four as the midday, the next forty-eight as the evening; hunger and thirst as consecration; austerity, giving, uprightness, non-injury and truthfulness as the priestly gifts; death as the final bath.
signs_of_progress: Mahidāsa Aitareya lived 116 years (ChU 3.16.7)
notes: Upaniṣadic 'vidyā' (meditation-knowledge); the Brahma Sūtra (3.3) discusses which vidyās are to be combined.

name: Service of the Lord's form (puṣṭi sevā)
method_summary: Loving, householder service of Kṛṣṇa's image (svarūpa) as a living child and lord — waking, feeding, dressing, playing, resting him — with body, wealth and above all the mind; the fruit of service is more service.

name: Spontaneous devotional practice (rāgānugā sādhana)
method_summary: Driven by eager longing for a Vraja resident's love, the practitioner continues external practice in the body while inwardly remembering Kṛṣṇa and the chosen associate and serving in the inner perfected body, living (physically or mentally) in Vraja and following those who love him.
prerequisites: eager longing (lobha)
guidance of a guru in the chosen mood

warnings.text: Semblances of emotion (ratyābhāsa) in those whose hearts are impure are not bhāva; outward signs alone do not prove love.

name: Rājasūya (royal consecration)
method_summary: The Śrauta consecration of a king, during which the story of Śunaḥśepa is recited (AB 7.13–18).
alt_method_summary: The soma rite consecrating a king, with the royal anointing and symbolic acts of sovereignty.

name: Recitation of the Rāma tāraka mantra
method_summary: Recitation of Rāma's mantra, the tāraka given at Avimukta (Rāmatāpanī; Rāmarahasya).

name: Expiatory and yogic recitation of the Raudrī Gāyatrī
method_summary: After seeing urine or faeces or speaking with women or śūdras, he touches water, performs breath-control and mutters the Raudrī Gāyatrī or the Bahurūpī; in the third stage recitation of the chosen Gāyatrī is the ground from which yoga proceeds.

name: Reflecting on the evil of birth, death, old age, disease and pain
method_summary: Constantly seeing the faults of birth, death, old age, disease and sorrow, one of the marks called knowledge (13.8).

name: Care of the dying (Purāṇic)
method_summary: Turning the dying person's mind to the Lord (remembrance, the name), gifts made by or for the dying (above all the Vaitaraṇī cow), and the recitation of sacred texts.
notes: Further customary acts (placing on the ground, sesame, Gaṅgā water, tulasī) are described in the Pretakalpa's later chapters; not checked verse by verse.

name: Ritual hand gestures (mudrā) of Āgamic worship
method_summary: Hand gestures shown to the deity at invocation, installation and offering, and in purificatory acts, named and described in the ritual manuals.

name: Constant remembrance of Rudra
method_summary: He always remembers Rudra and, cutting with the intellect the root of the net of causes of faults, fixes the whole mind on Rudra.

name: Recitation of the Śatarudrīya with the Camaka (Rudra-japa)
method_summary: Chanting the Namaka (homage to Rudra in all forms) with the Camaka (petitions 'for me'), singly or in multiples — traditionally eleven recitations (ekādaśa-rudra), 121 (laghu-rudra), 1,331 (mahā-rudra), 14,641 (ati-rudra); in the agnicayana the Śatarudrīya pacifies Rudra.
notes: The multiples are recalled from living practice literature (moderate confidence).

name: Rudrābhiṣeka (bathing the liṅga with the Rudram)
method_summary: Bathing an image or liṅga of Śiva with water, milk and other substances while the Śatarudrīya is chanted — a later temple and domestic worship that employs the Saṃhitā litany.
notes: Post-Saṃhitā usage (Āgamic/Purāṇic setting); only the Vedic mantra element is U01's.

name: Wearing rudrākṣa
method_summary: Wearing rudrākṣa beads of specified faces and numbers on the crown, head, throat, arms and wrists; one of the eight shields; at death rudrākṣa-water is drunk while thinking of Rudra.
alt_method_summary: Wearing beads of chosen size, colour and number of faces, consecrated with mantras, observing food and conduct rules (Rudrākṣajābāla).

name: Meditation on the deity's form
method_summary: Holding the mind on the form of the Lord in the heart or before the mind's eye, limb by limb from the feet to the smiling face, until it does not waver; then simplifying the form (without weapons, without ornaments, one limb) or dwelling on the face (BhP 2.2.8-14; 3.28.12-33; VP 6.7.75-90).
stage: intermediate; after ethical preparation, posture and breath
prerequisites: yama and niyama
mastery of posture and breath
withdrawal of the senses
signs_of_progress: the form stays in mind whether walking, standing or acting (VP 6.7.87)

name: The teaching of being (sad-vidyā)
method_summary: Uddālaka's method: by one lump of clay all clay is known; in the beginning was being alone; it made heat, water and food threefold; illustrated by sleep, dying, honey, rivers, the tree, the banyan seed, salt, the blindfolded man and the axe ordeal, each ending 'that you are'.
notes: Upaniṣadic 'vidyā' (meditation-knowledge); the Brahma Sūtra (3.3) discusses which vidyās are to be combined.

name: The daily routine of right conduct (sadācāra)
method_summary: Rising while remembering Hari, purification, cleaning the teeth, sipping water, bathing according to rule, the twilight rites, worship and study, all acts dedicated to Acyuta.

name: The six-limbed yoga of the Maitrī
method_summary: Breath-control, withdrawal of the senses, meditation, concentration, contemplative reasoning (tarka) and absorption; the text adds placing the mind in the no-mind and the breath in the fourth (6.19), a concentration by restraining speech, mind and breath with a gesture of the tongue at the palate, seeing brahman by tarka (6.20), and rising through the suṣumṇā joined with breath, Om and mind (6.21).
signs_of_progress: seeing the golden-coloured maker; faults do not approach the knower, as animals avoid a burning mountain (6.18); becoming selfless (nirātman), the mark of liberation (6.20)

equivalents.note: shares prāṇāyāma, pratyāhāra, dhyāna, dhāraṇā and samādhi with Patañjali's limbs but has tarka and a different order

notes: Recorded as the text states it; later haṭha elaborations of the palate practice (khecarī) are restricted and belong to other units. Distinct from the Kālacakra six-branch yoga.

name: The seven aids as disciplines
method_summary: Purity of food, freedom from desire, repeated practice, performance of the five great sacrifices and other duties, the virtues (truthfulness, uprightness, compassion, generosity, non-injury, non-covetousness), freedom from dejection and from elation.

name: Sadyaḥsamutkrānti: initiation bringing immediate departure
method_summary: A rite described in Tantrāloka 19 by which the teacher releases a qualified disciple from the body at once into Śiva. Summary only; no procedure is given here.

warnings.text: Treated in the tantra as reserved to the qualified teacher and disciple (details not recorded here).

notes: Restricted (a rite ending bodily life). Content from the chapter title and table of contents only.

name: Meditation with and without qualities
method_summary: Meditation on a form (the Lord in the heart, Maheśvara as oneself) or on the Self's nature without form, leading to samādhi (Yogatattva 104; Śāṇḍilya 1.71; Darśana 9).

name: Meditation on the qualified Brahman (saguṇa-upāsanā)
method_summary: Sustained meditation on Brahman with attributes or through a symbol (Oṃ, the sun, the mind), seated, one-pointed, in any suitable place, continued until death; leads to the Brahma-world and gradual liberation, and prepares the mind for knowledge.

name: Sahita-kumbhaka (sūryabheda, ujjāyī, śītalī, bhastrī)
method_summary: Retention joined with inhalation and exhalation, in four named varieties (Yogakuṇḍalī 1.19ff.). Summary only; no counts.

warnings.text: Breath must be tamed gradually, like a lion, elephant or tiger; otherwise it kills the practitioner; improper practice causes hiccup, asthma, cough and pains of head, ears and eyes.

name: Funeral rites for Śaiva initiates (antyeṣṭi)
method_summary: Special funeral rites for initiates in which the guru ritually completes the soul's release; described in the Siddhānta paddhatis.

name: Caryā (Śaiva temple service)
method_summary: Service of Śiva in the temple with the body: sweeping and smearing the floor, gathering flowers and making garlands, lighting lamps, singing the hymns, serving devotees — in the attitude of a servant (dāsa-mārga), as Appar did.
signs_of_progress: the fruit is sālokya, dwelling in Śiva's world

name: Śaiva meditation with and without object
method_summary: Meditation on Śiva's form (Śrīkaṇṭha) first, with an object and a seed, and at the end without object or seed, as awareness of the formless self; knowing the meditator, the act, the object and the purpose.

name: Jñāna (knowledge of Śiva)
method_summary: Knowledge given by grace through the guru, cultivated in four steps: hearing (kēṭṭal), reflecting (cintittal), clarity (teḷital) and abiding (niṭṭai); seeing the tattvas and the soul as not-Śiva and the world as a mirage, meditating the five letters, abiding at Śiva's feet — the true path (san-mārga).
signs_of_progress: fruit: sāyujya, union

name: Kriyā (Śaiva ritual worship)
method_summary: Worship of Śiva in the liṅga or image with the prescribed mantras, offerings and fire — the son's attitude (satputra-mārga), as Campantar's.
prerequisites: initiation (dīkṣā)
signs_of_progress: fruit: sāmīpya, nearness to Śiva

name: Pilgrimage to the Tēvāram shrines
method_summary: Visiting and singing at the shrines praised in the Tēvāram (the 274 'sung places', pāṭal peṟṟa talam) and at Chidambaram, following the saints' journeys.

name: Hymn-devotion to Śiva as one's own self
method_summary: Praising Śiva with hymns in which the devotee relishes an identity already recognized; for one rich in devotion Śiva manifests without meditation, mantra or procedure (Śivastotrāvalī 1.1; Abhinavagupta's Bhairavastava).

name: Yoga (Śivayoga)
method_summary: Inner worship and meditation on Śiva: the Āgamas' six-limbed yoga (breath control, withdrawal, holding, meditation, reasoning [tarka], absorption) or the Tirumantiram's eight limbs, fixing the mind on Śiva in the heart or at the centres — the friend's attitude (sakhā-mārga), as Cuntarar's.
signs_of_progress: fruit: sārūpya, Śiva's form

warnings.text: The powers that arise from yoga are not the goal; only knowledge by grace gives final release.

name: Abiding as the witness (sākṣi-bhāva)
method_summary: Recognizing oneself as the unchanging witness of the mind's modes, the senses and the states, like the lamp in a theatre that lights all and remains when all have gone.

name: Resting as the witness (Aṣṭāvakra Gītā)
method_summary: Knowing oneself as the witness of the elements, body and mind, separating from the body and resting in consciousness, one is free now.

warnings.text: The practice of samādhi itself is called bondage from the absolute standpoint (1.15).

name: Contraction of power (śaktisaṅkoca)
method_summary: Withdrawing the flow of the senses from their objects and turning back toward the source, like a tortoise drawing in its limbs (Kṣemarāja's auto-commentary on Pratyabhijñāhṛdaya 18; summary).

name: Expansion of power (śaktivikāsa); the bhairavī seal
method_summary: Keeping awareness within while the eyes and senses remain open to objects without blinking - 'attention inward, gaze outward' - so that the senses open simultaneously into consciousness (Kṣemarāja's auto-commentary on Pratyabhijñāhṛdaya 18, which quotes the bhairavī mudrā; summary).

name: Śakticālana (moving the power)
method_summary: Rousing the kuṇḍalinī from her place and leading her upward through the suṣumnā, with sarasvatī-cālana; the texts say it removes abdominal disease. Summary only.

name: Sāman chanting (sāmagāna)
method_summary: Singing the verses of the Sāmaveda to their melodies as given in the song-books — village and forest songs and their ritual applications — with stretched vowels, repetitions and stobhas, the notes shown on the fingers; at the soma rite the udgātṛ, prastotṛ and pratihartṛ divide the parts.
prerequisites: initiation in a Sāmaveda śākhā

warnings.text: A mantra wrong in accent or letter does not convey its meaning; as a verbal thunderbolt it harms the sacrificer, as 'Indra-śatru' did through a fault of accent.
The forest (āraṇyageya) melodies are regarded as potent and are learned apart, outside the village (as reported).

name: Samādhi as the eighth limb
method_summary: Meditation shining only as its object, as if empty of its own form (3.3, YBh 3.3).
alt_method_summary: Lineage contribution (Upaniṣadic): the sixth limb of the Maitrī's yoga (6.18); 'the happiness of a mind whose stains are washed away by samādhi cannot be described' (MaiU 6.34); being 'collected' (samāhita) in BAU 4.4.23 and KU 1.2.24.

name: Offering before use (samarpaṇa)
method_summary: Nothing unoffered is used: food, clothes and all things are first offered to the Lord and then accepted as his grace.

name: Samāvartana (return home, final bath)
method_summary: The ceremonial bath (snāna) ending studentship, after which the graduate (snātaka) may marry; he keeps the snātaka rules (MDh 4).

name: Initiation into the observances (samaya-dīkṣā)
method_summary: First Śaiva initiation making the disciple a samayin, bound by post-initiatory rules and entitled to worship and study; for the incapable, the observances may be purified away (seedless initiation).
alt_method_summary: The first initiation, conferring the status of samayin with rules of conduct and the right to worship and study.

name: Śāmbhava immersion
method_summary: Immersion (samāveśa) that arises for one who thinks of nothing, awakened by the teacher: consciousness rests in itself without thought-constructs, the universe seen as a reflection in the mirror of consciousness (MVT 2.23; TĀ 1.168, 3).

name: Śāmbhavī mudrā
method_summary: Gazing with open, unblinking eyes while attention rests on the inner target; three forms by the eyes' opening (amā, pratipat, pūrṇimā), the open 'full-moon' gaze being recommended.
signs_of_progress: the place where such a yogin lives is purified (Advayatāraka)

name: Meditation on combinations (saṃhitā)
method_summary: Meditate on the five great combinations — of worlds, lights, knowledge, progeny and the body — each as prior form, latter form, junction and link (TU 1.3).

name: The means-accomplishments: study, hearing, reasoning, friends, giving
method_summary: Five of the eight accomplishments of SK 51 serve as means to knowledge of the principles: studying the texts, hearing instruction, examining by reasoning ('what is true, what is highest, what is the final good'), gaining a friend or fellow student who knows, and serving the venerable with gifts (Gauḍapāda) — Vācaspati (recalled) reads dāna as the purification of discriminative knowledge. Approaching a teacher to end the three sufferings is itself an accomplishment.
prerequisites: desire to know born of suffering (SK 1)
signs_of_progress: knowledge of the twenty-five principles arises

warnings.text: Error, incapacity and contentment are the curb that holds the world in ignorance like a goaded elephant; they must be abandoned.
Hearing without reflection does not bring fulfilment, as with Virocana.

equivalents.note: hearing/study (śabda, adhyayana) ~ Advaita's śravaṇa (interpretive)
reasoning (ūha) ~ Advaita's manana (interpretive)

name: Rites for concord (sāṃmanasya)
method_summary: Rites with the concord hymns to make family and assembly of one heart and mind.

name: Renunciation (saṃnyāsa) in the Dharmaśāstra
method_summary: After the Prājāpatya sacrifice with all possessions given away, the renouncer deposits the fires in himself and goes forth giving safety to all beings; he lives alone, without fire or house, begging once a day, purifying step, water, speech and act, delighting in the self, practising breath-control and meditation, neither welcoming death nor life (MDh 6.33–85); he must not renounce the Veda (VDh 10.4).
stage: after the debts are paid (or, in other views, from any stage)

warnings.text: Seeking liberation without paying the three debts leads downward (MDh 6.35–37).

name: The father-to-son transfer at death (sampratti)
method_summary: A dying father transfers his roles and faculties to his son: 'you are brahman, the sacrifice, the world' (BAU 1.5.17); or lying on the son and placing speech, breath, sight and the other faculties in him one by one, the son receiving each (KauU 2.15).

name: Vaikhānasa image worship (samūrtārcana)
method_summary: Daily worship of Viṣṇu with Vedic mantras: eight services to the fixed image by flowers only, thirty-two services to the movable (kautuka) image, invoking the five forms, with fire offering.

name: Discussion with the learned (saṃvāda)
method_summary: Discussion with pupils, teachers, fellow-students and distinguished seekers of the good who are free of envy — even without advancing one's own counter-thesis — for the ripening of wisdom: cutting doubt, understanding the unknown, confirming what has been ascertained.
signs_of_progress: doubt cut
the unknown understood
what is ascertained confirmed (NBh 4.2.47)

name: The meditation on the gatherer (saṃvarga-vidyā)
method_summary: Venerate wind as the gatherer into which fire, sun, moon and waters go (with respect to the gods) and breath as the gatherer into which speech, sight, hearing and mind go in sleep (with respect to the self).
notes: Upaniṣadic 'vidyā' (meditation-knowledge); the Brahma Sūtra (3.3) discusses which vidyās are to be combined.

name: Saṃyama
method_summary: Concentration, meditation and samādhi together on one object (3.4), applied stage by stage (3.6) to objects such as the three transformations, the sun, moon, pole star, navel wheel, throat-well, heart, the moment and its sequence (3.16–52).
signs_of_progress: the light of insight (3.5); the powers (3.16–49)

warnings.text: The powers are obstacles in samādhi; they are powers only in the emergent state.
Invited by the celestials, form neither attachment nor pride, for the undesired would recur.
Without mastering the lower stage one does not gain saṃyama on higher stages by skipping.

name: Saṃyamas for powers (Śāṇḍilya)
method_summary: Concentration on parts of the body, on merit and demerit, on the throat, the kūrma-nāḍī, the light in the head and so on, each yielding a power.

name: Sandhyā (twilight worship)
method_summary: At dawn and dusk: sipping and bathing, sprinkling with the water-verses, breath-control with the Gāyatrī, offering water to the sun (which scatters the Mandeha demons, TA 2.2), and reciting the Sāvitrī standing till sunrise or sitting till the stars appear (YS 1.22–25); the sun is meditated on as Brahman.
alt_method_summary: The daily worship at the junctions of the day by the initiated: purification with water, the sin-effacing verses (RV 10.190), offerings of water to the sun, and repetition of the Gāyatrī.
notes: U01 contribution: its Saṃhitā mantras. The rite's structure is set out in gṛhya/dharma texts (U02).

name: Śāṇḍilya's meditation (Śāṇḍilya-vidyā)
method_summary: In tranquillity, venerate all this as brahman — that from which it arises, into which it dissolves and by which it breathes; form one's resolve, since one becomes on departing what one resolves here; meditate on the self in the heart, made of mind, with breath as body and light as form, smaller than a grain and greater than the worlds, as brahman to be attained on departing, without doubt.
notes: Upaniṣadic 'vidyā' (meditation-knowledge); the Brahma Sūtra (3.3) discusses which vidyās are to be combined.

name: Śāṇḍilya-vidyā (meditation on the self made of mind)
method_summary: Resolving that one becomes at death what one's resolve is, one meditates on the self as made of mind, with breath for body, of the form of light, small as a grain within and greater than all worlds, and resolves to attain it on departing (ŚB 10.6.3; ChU 3.14).

name: Renunciation (saṃnyāsa)
method_summary: Rising above the desires for sons, wealth and worlds, living as a mendicant on alms, wandering forth for the sake of the self (BAU 3.5.1, 4.4.22); ascetics purified by the yoga of renunciation (MuU 3.2.6); forest-dwelling with austerity and faith on alms (MuU 1.2.11); after the father-son transfer the recovered father may wander as a mendicant (KauU 2.15).
notes: The rules of the renunciant orders are in the Saṃnyāsa Upaniṣads (U04) and later texts (U57).

name: The renunciation rite (saṃnyāsa-dīkṣā)
method_summary: Penances, śrāddhas (including for oneself), the virajā homa, placing the fires in oneself, the declaration of renunciation said three times, the gift of fearlessness, abandoning topknot and thread (or not, in the Vaiṣṇava rite), receiving staff and cloth, and the teaching of praṇava and great saying.
prerequisites: dispassion; the fourfold means; eligibility; consent of kin (varies by text)

name: Pacificatory rites (śānti)
method_summary: Rites appeasing portents, planets and harmful powers with the peace hymns.

name: Peace chants (śānti-pāṭha)
method_summary: Reciting peace invocations at the beginning and end of study and rites: 'may we hear with our ears what is auspicious' (RV 1.89.8), 'may Mitra be propitious to us' (1.90.9), 'peace be heaven, peace the atmosphere …' (VS 36.17), 'peaceful be heaven, peaceful the earth' (AVŚ 19.9).

name: Contentment (saṃtoṣa)
method_summary: Not wanting more than the means at hand (YBh 2.32).
signs_of_progress: unsurpassed happiness (2.42)

name: Sapiṇḍīkaraṇa
method_summary: The rite that unites the preta's piṇḍa with those of father, grandfather and great-grandfather, ending the preta state; preferably on the twelfth day, or after three fortnights, six months or a year.
alt_method_summary: The rite that merges the piṇḍa of the newly dead with those of his three forefathers, making the preta a pitṛ (on the twelfth day or at the end of the first year, by different authorities).

name: The seven subtle dhāraṇās (MkP 40)
method_summary: Holding the mind at the head on earth, water, fire, air, space, mind and intellect in turn, experiencing and then abandoning the subtlety of each, without attachment to any.

warnings.text: Attachment to any element's subtlety destroys the yogin and he returns (to rebirth).

name: Taking refuge in the Lord alone (śaraṇāgati)
method_summary: Abandoning all dharmas, take refuge in the Lord alone, who frees from all sins (18.66); take refuge in him with one's whole being (18.62); coming once for refuge, saying 'I am yours', one is granted freedom from fear (Rāmāyaṇa 6.18.33).
notes: Interpreted variously by the schools (see dsp:gita-primary-teaching); U05's contribution to a practice systematized by U14.
alt_method_summary: Lineage contribution (Upaniṣadic): 'I, desiring liberation, go for refuge to that God who illumines the understanding of the self' (ŚU 6.18).

The seeker takes refuge in the Lord (or in Śrī) as the sole means, with the resolve to do what pleases him, avoidance of what displeases, faith that he will protect, choosing him as protector, laying down oneself and helplessness; thereafter free of grief and fear, without 'mine' or ego.

equivalents.note: Śrīvaiṣṇava prapatti rests on these texts

name: Renunciation of everything (sarva-tyāga)
method_summary: True renunciation is the giving up of the mind itself, the root of all; outer renunciation of kingdom or belongings does not suffice while the notion 'I renounce' remains.

name: Forgetting everything (Aṣṭāvakra Gītā)
method_summary: Abiding in oneself comes not from studying many scriptures but from forgetting everything.

name: Cultivation of the six virtues (ṣaṭ-sampatti)
method_summary: Practising calm, self-control, withdrawal, forbearance, faith and concentration as auxiliaries of knowledge (BS 3.4.27; BĀU 4.4.23).

name: Recitation of the Śatarudrīya
method_summary: Recitation of the Rudra hymn of the Yajurveda; 'these are the names of immortality' (Jābāla 3); by it one becomes atyāśramin and reaches kaivalya (Kaivalya 2).

name: Holy company (satsaṅga)
method_summary: Seeking out and serving the holy, hearing the talks that arise in their company; the Yoga Vāsiṣṭha's fourth gatekeeper, the Bhāgavata's means that wins the Lord, the first of the Adhyātma Rāmāyaṇa's nine means.
signs_of_progress: faith, attraction and devotion arise in order (Kapila Gītā 3.25.25)

name: Sattarka: purification of thought by pure reasoning (śākta means)
method_summary: Thought-constructs are purified (vikalpa-saṃskāra) by pure reasoning (sattarka), the teacher's instruction and scripture, repeatedly affirming the pure thought 'I am Śiva, all this is my glory' until it becomes thought-free (TĀ 4; MVT 2.22).

name: Sāttvic food
method_summary: Prefer foods that increase life, vitality, strength, health, happiness and cheerfulness, that are savoury, oily, substantial and agreeable; avoid the bitter, sour, salty, very hot, pungent, dry and burning (rājasic) and the stale, tasteless, putrid, leftover and impure (tāmasic) (17.7–10).

name: Relinquishment before action (sāttvika-tyāga)
method_summary: Before any act, relinquishing the sense of agency, of ownership and desire for its fruit: 'the Lord himself, for his own sake, has this done through me'.

name: Truthfulness (satya)
method_summary: Speech and mind according to fact, spoken for the good of all beings after examination (YBh 2.30).
signs_of_progress: actions and their fruits rest on one's word (2.36)

warnings.text: Truth spoken to harm beings is not truth but sin, a semblance of merit leading to painful darkness.

alt_method_summary: Lineage contribution (Upaniṣadic): 'speak the truth' (TU 1.11.1); truth alone conquers (MuU 3.1.6); truthful speech among the priestly gifts (ChU 3.17.4); the truthful is not burned (ChU 6.16).

name: Purity (śauca)
method_summary: Outer purity with earth, water and pure food, and inner washing away of the mind's stains (YBh 2.32).
signs_of_progress: disgust for one's own body, non-contact with others; purity of sattva, cheerfulness, one-pointedness, mastery of the senses, fitness to see the self (2.40–41)

name: Sautrāmaṇī
method_summary: A rite to Indra the good protector (sutrāman) with offerings including surā, performed for healing and restoration.

name: Savikalpa samādhi (Vedānta)
method_summary: Absorption with the mental mode resting in Brahman while the distinction of knower and known remains; with inner and outer forms, attended by objects or by words (Dṛg-Dṛśya Viveka).

warnings.text: Relishing its bliss (rasāsvāda) obstructs nirvikalpa samādhi.

name: Seeing the Lord in all beings and bowing to all
method_summary: Regarding every being as the Lord, with equal vision toward brāhmaṇa and outcaste, prostrating even to dog, outcaste, cow and donkey, ignoring others' laughter, until the vision of the Lord in all arises; images are worshipped only until the Lord is known in one's own heart and in all beings.

name: Serving one's parents as dharma
method_summary: The meat-seller serves his aged parents as gods and sends Kauśika home to serve his own (MBh 3.204–206).

name: Closing the senses (ṣaṇmukhī)
method_summary: Closing ears, eyes and other openings with the fingers so that the inner sounds are heard.
signs_of_progress: sounds like bells (Yogacūḍāmaṇi 114–115)

name: Concentrations yielding the siddhis (Uddhava Gītā)
method_summary: Kṛṣṇa describes, for each of the eighteen powers, a concentration of the mind on a particular aspect of the Lord; summarized here without the individual procedures.

warnings.text: The siddhis are obstacles and a waste of time for one practising the highest yoga; the goal of yoga is not reached by them.

name: Sīmantonnayana (parting of the hair)
method_summary: A rite in the later months of pregnancy in which the husband parts the wife's hair for her and the child's protection.

name: The head-vow (śirovrata)
method_summary: A vow whose performance, 'according to rule', qualifies one to be taught the knowledge of brahman (MuU 3.2.10-11); the text does not describe it.
notes: Commentators differ on its nature; not reconstructed here.

name: Recitation of Śiva mantras
method_summary: Recitation of Śiva's five- or six-syllable mantra and of Dakṣiṇāmūrti's mantras (Pañcabrahma; Bhasmajābāla; Dakṣiṇāmūrti).

name: Recitation of the thousand names of Śiva (Mahābhārata)
method_summary: Reciting the thousand names of Śiva that Upamanyu taught Kṛṣṇa (MBh 13.14–17).

name: Śivānubhava — shared discourse on experience
method_summary: Devotees gather to speak from and test their experience of Śiva in dialogue, as the śaraṇas did in the Anubhava Maṇṭapa; continued in modern maṭhas as 'śivānubhava' gatherings.

name: The Śivarātri vow
method_summary: Fast and night-long vigil with worship of the liṅga on Śiva's night; the hunter who kept it unknowingly was saved.

name: Śivayoga-samādhi
method_summary: Through inner worship, meditation on Śiva as one's self: the supreme self is contemplated in the haṃsa form with the feeling 'I am He' until attention is undivided; the six centres are contemplated from the base to the brows and Śambhu in the aperture called Kailāsa within the thousand-petalled lotus.

warnings.text: The breath element (meeting of prāṇa and apāna) is done on the teacher's instruction (commentary on 12.6); no method is recorded here.

name: The sixty-four limbs of devotional practice
method_summary: Rūpa's list of practices: the first ten (taking shelter of a guru, initiation and instruction, serving the guru with trust, following the saints, inquiring into true dharma, renouncing enjoyment for Kṛṣṇa, residence at holy places, accepting only what is needed, honouring Ekādaśī, honouring the sacred trees, cows and brāhmaṇas) and ten avoidances (of non-devotees' company, many disciples, great undertakings, many books for argument, miserliness, grief, disrespect of other gods, harming beings, offences in worship and to the name, tolerating blasphemy) are the gateway; then hearing, chanting, remembering, worship, bowing, prayer, service, friendship, self-offering, wearing Vaiṣṇava marks, honouring prasāda, tulasī, festivals and more, ending with the five most potent limbs.
notes: The full list of sixty-four is recalled only in part; verse-by-verse list to be extracted in Phase D.

name: Constant remembrance of the Lord (smaraṇa)
method_summary: Remember the Lord at all times, with mind and intellect fixed on him, even while acting (8.7); the yogin who remembers him constantly with undivided mind finds him easily attained (8.14).

name: Dwelling in the cremation ground
method_summary: In the fourth stage he lives in the cremation ground, in the open or at the foot of a tree, not leaving it until the body falls, living on what comes unasked, practising remembrance.
signs_of_progress: union with Rudra (the stated gain)

name: Satyakāma's meditation on the four quarters of brahman
method_summary: Venerate brahman as having four quarters of four parts each — the quarters of space ('shining'), earth, mid-space, sky and ocean ('endless'), fire, sun, moon and lightning ('luminous'), breath, sight, hearing and mind ('having an abode') — as taught to Satyakāma by a bull, fire, a goose and a diver-bird.
notes: Names of the quarters from memory (moderate). Upaniṣadic 'vidyā' (meditation-knowledge); the Brahma Sūtra (3.3) discusses which vidyās are to be combined.

name: Spanda awareness
method_summary: Being constantly intent on discerning the spanda principle, one attains one's own nature even while awake; spanda is to be grasped in intense states (great anger, joy, perplexity, running) and in the opening (unmeṣa) from which a new thought arises in one absorbed in a single thought (SK 1.21-22, 3.9).

warnings.text: Light, sound, form and taste that arise from the unmeṣa agitate the embodied (read as a caution against distraction by them).
A void, sleep-like absorption is artificial and not the principle (SK 1.12-13).

name: Feigned trembling (spandana)
method_summary: He deliberately shakes his limbs as if struck by a wind-disorder.

warnings.text: Undertaken only after knowledge has been gained, impurity reduced and the teacher's permission obtained; the feigned acts must not conflict with the restraints (non-harming, celibacy etc.).

name: Śrāddha
method_summary: Rites of faith for the dead and the ancestors - ekoddiṣṭa for the preta, the sixteen śrāddhas, monthly and annual rites, pārvaṇa for the three ancestors - with feeding of brahmins; they feed the dead on Yama's road and satisfy the ancestors.

name: Śrāddha (offering to the ancestors)
