method_summary: Qualified brāhmaṇas are invited and fed as the ancestors' representatives, rice-balls (piṇḍa) are offered to the father, grandfather and great-grandfather, and water and sesame given; performed monthly at the new moon and on death-anniversaries and other occasions (MDh 3.122–286).

name: The śrauta sacrifice (in general)
method_summary: Solemn rites performed in three fires (gārhapatya, āhavanīya, dakṣiṇāgni) by priests of the Vedas — hotṛ (Ṛgveda), adhvaryu (Yajurveda), udgātṛ (Sāmaveda) and brahmán (overseer), up to sixteen in the great soma rites — for a patron (yajamāna) and his wife, with oblations, recitations, chants and gifts (dakṣiṇā).
prerequisites: initiated householder, married, who has established the fires

name: Hearing the scriptures (śravaṇa)
method_summary: Study of scripture and its right interpretation under a teacher. In Dvaita: hearing the true scriptures (Vedas, Mahābhārata, Pañcarātra, Purāṇas) with Madhva's commentaries so as to know Viṣṇu's supremacy, the five differences and gradation; the first principal means to knowledge, never to be curtailed.
stage: all (the lowest adhikārin qualifies by study and devotion)
prerequisites: devotion to Viṣṇu
a qualified teacher
eligibility by class and qualities (adhikāra)
sādhana-catuṣṭaya
a teacher (śrotriya, brahmaniṣṭha)
alt_method_summary: Systematic study of the Upaniṣads (with the Gītā and Brahma Sūtras) under a qualified teacher, determining by the six marks of purport that their meaning is the non-dual Brahman; for the Vivaraṇa the principal means, for one of sharp understanding sufficient by itself.
Lineage contribution (Upaniṣadic): 'the self should be seen, heard, reflected upon and meditated upon'; hearing is the second of the four verbs (BAU 2.4.5, 4.5.6).
signs_of_progress: doubt about what scripture teaches is removed (pramāṇa-saṃśaya)

name: Offering to the deity's attendants (śrībhūtabali)
method_summary: Offering of cooked rice on the stones of the deity's attendant beings and guardians placed around the shrine, with the festival image carried in procession.

name: Contemplation of the body as the Śrīcakra
method_summary: The body's openings, channels, winds and faculties contemplated as the enclosures and deities of the Śrīcakra; worship as contemplation of non-difference (Bhāvanā; Tripurā).

name: Feigned amorous gestures (śṛṅgāraṇa)
method_summary: Standing at a distance from a group of women, he looks at one young woman and makes signs of desire such as arranging his hair, so as to be called unchaste; the act is a pretence.

warnings.text: Undertaken only after knowledge has been gained, impurity reduced and the teacher's permission obtained; the feigned acts must not conflict with the restraints (non-harming, celibacy etc.).

name: Sthānakalpanā: positing places (breath, body, outer)
method_summary: The lowest āṇava support: positing the divine in 'places' - in the breath and its time-cycles (TĀ 6), in the body, and in outer supports such as the liṅga or maṇḍala.

name: Recitation of the tradition's hymns
method_summary: Daily recitation of Madhva's Dvādaśastotra and Narasiṃhanakhastuti and Trivikrama's Vāyustuti (framed by the Narasiṃha verses); in the Rāghavendra tradition, the Rāghavendra hymn.

name: Holding the mind on the auspicious support (VP 6.7)
method_summary: With breath and senses mastered, fix the mind on Viṣṇu's form as the ground of all powers, simplifying it stage by stage, until dhyāna (a single continuous flow) and samādhi (grasping the object's own nature free of imagination) arise.

name: Dwelling in an empty house or cave
method_summary: In the stage of conquest he lives in an empty house or cave free from distraction, constantly with the god, senses conquered, studying and meditating.
duration: six months of constant yoga are named for the powers to arise (PS 5.12-13)
signs_of_progress: powers such as distant sight arise gradually

name: Worship of the deity in a pot of liquor (reported)
method_summary: Summary only: opponents report that the Kālāmukhas set up a pot of liquor and worship the deity placed in it.

name: Self-study (svādhyāya)
method_summary: Repetition of the praṇava and other purifying formulas, or study of scriptures on liberation (YBh 2.1, 2.32); repetition of mantras preceded by the praṇava (RM 2.1).
signs_of_progress: contact with the chosen deity; gods, sages and siddhas appear (2.44, YBh 2.44)
alt_method_summary: Daily recitation of one's Veda, at least a portion, as the sacrifice to Brahman (ŚB 11.5.6.3; TA 2.10); it brings concentration, independence, sound sleep and delight in the one thing (ŚB 11.5.7.1).
Lineage contribution (Upaniṣadic): every duty is to be joined with study and teaching of the Veda; 'study and teaching alone, for that is austerity' (TU 1.9); 'do not neglect your study' (TU 1.11).

warnings.text: Recitation is suspended on the prescribed non-study occasions (anadhyāya).

name: Performing one's own duty (svakarma)
method_summary: One's own duty is performing the acts enjoined for one's stage of life; with concentration and posture it supports meditation (SS 3.32, 3.35).

name: Support in the knowledge of dream and sleep (1.38)
method_summary: Letting the mind rest on the knowledge of dream or of sleep as its support, taking that form (1.38, YBh 1.38).

name: Dwelling on one's own nature (svasvarūpānusandhāna) as devotion
method_summary: Devotion understood as continuous attention to one's own true nature (VC 31), the chief among the means to liberation.

name: The yoga of the Śvetāśvatara (posture, breath, place)
method_summary: Hold the body steady with chest, neck and head erect; draw the senses with the mind into the heart; restrain the breaths, with movements controlled, and breathe out gently through the nose when the breath is diminished; hold the mind attentively like a chariot yoked to unruly horses; practise in a level, clean place free of pebbles, fire, sand, noise and damp, pleasing to the mind and sheltered from wind.
prerequisites: the invocations of Savitṛ to yoke the mind (ŚU 2.1-7)
signs_of_progress: forms like fog, smoke, sun, wind, fire, fireflies, lightning, crystal and moon precede brahman's manifestation; lightness, health, freedom from craving, clear complexion, pleasant voice and smell, scant excreta (ŚU 2.11-13)

warnings.text: The place must be free of disturbances (pebbles, fire, sand, noise, water-places) and not offend the eye (ŚU 2.10).
The breath is to be let out gently through the nose when diminished (ŚU 2.9).

name: Śyena (a sorcery rite)
method_summary: A rite the Veda states as the means for one who wishes to harm an enemy. Mīmāṃsā records it only to show that the Veda does not enjoin harming: the rite is described as a means, not as a duty.

warnings.text: The Śyena and similar rites (Vajra, Iṣu) are harmful (anartha): their aim is violence, violence is prohibited, and they lead to sin (pratyavāya); they are not dharma.

notes: Summary only (abhicāra rite).

name: Austerity (tapas)
method_summary: Bearing the pairs of opposites — hunger and thirst, cold and heat, standing and sitting, silence — with vows as suitable (YBh 2.32); it breaks up impurity, without which yoga does not succeed (YBh 2.1). Summary only: the fasting vows the bhāṣya names (kṛcchra, cāndrāyaṇa, sāntapana) are not described here.
signs_of_progress: perfection of body and senses through the destruction of impurity (2.43)

warnings.text: It should be practised so as not to disturb the clarity of the mind (tac ca cittaprasādanam abādhamānam anenāsevyam).
Lopāmudrā's complaint that many autumns of toil wear away the body, and the resolution that tapas and married life together bear fruit, are the Saṃhitā's own counterweight to one-sided austerity.
Rites and austerities performed without knowing the imperishable come to an end (BAU 3.8.10).

notes: Marked restricted because it includes prolonged fasting vows; summary and the text's own warning only.
alt_method_summary: Ascetic exertion that 'heats' the practitioner: by it the ancients reached heaven, the seers were born, the student fills the worlds; the Vrātya stands upright for a year; the unheated cannot attain soma.

Lineage contribution (Upaniṣadic): Bhṛgu seeks brahman by tapas (TU 3.1-6); a year of austerity, celibacy and faith before questioning (PrU 1.2); the self is found by truth and austerity (MuU 3.1.5; ŚU 1.15); austerity as a branch of dharma (ChU 2.23.1).
Enduring pain and harming none (Kuṟaḷ ch. 27).
alt_notes: Extreme austerities are not described in method; none of the Saṃhitā passages gives steps.

name: Wearing Viṣṇu's heated emblems (tapta-mudrā-dhāraṇa)
method_summary: Summary only: the Mādhva tradition marks the body with Viṣṇu's discus and conch emblems, either heated or in clay; heated emblems are received at set times of the year and at the thread ceremony in the presence of the maṭha's head.
notes: Restricted: involves marking the body with heated metal; no procedure recorded. Its legitimacy was contested by Smārta critics and defended by Mādhva authors (a work 'Cakramīmāṃsā' is ascribed to Vijayīndra) — recalled at low confidence.

name: Tāraka-yoga
method_summary: Meditation on the 'crossing' light between the brows through the three targets and the voids, proceeding from tāraka with form to tāraka without form and to the mind-less (amanaska) state.
prerequisites: renouncer endowed with the six qualities (Advayatāraka)

name: Discriminating the principles (Sāṃkhya in the Mokṣadharma)
method_summary: Enumerating the twenty-four principles of prakṛti and knowing the twenty-fifth as other than them, the knower awakens and becomes alone (MBh 12.294); knowing the faults of body, senses and guṇas, the Sāṃkhya follower is freed (12.290).

name: Repeated practice of the principles (tattvābhyāsa)
method_summary: After hearing the principles (manifest, unmanifest, knower) from scripture and teacher and establishing them by reasoning, one contemplates them repeatedly — long, reverently and without interruption — discriminating puruṣa from each principle and renouncing identification with each ('not this, not this'), until the knowledge 'I am not, not mine, not I' arises.
prerequisites: hearing and reasoning about the twenty-five principles; dispassion
duration: long and uninterrupted; Vācaspati speaks of many births of practice
signs_of_progress: the complete, pure, single knowledge 'I am not, not mine, not I' (SK 64); prakṛti seen as by a spectator, having ceased (SK 65–66)

warnings.text: Liberation is not attained by mere hearing, because beginningless latent tendencies are strong.
Dispassion without discrimination leads only to absorption in prakṛti, from which one rises again.

equivalents.note: long uninterrupted contemplation after hearing and reflection, as in Advaita's nididhyāsana; content and goal differ (discrimination vs identity)

name: Temple-building rites from ploughing to installation (karṣaṇādi)
method_summary: Examination and taking possession of the site, ploughing (karṣaṇa), sprouting seeds, laying out the ground-plan (vāstu-maṇḍala), offerings to the site deities, deposit of the foundation (garbhanyāsa), and rites at each stage of construction up to installation; the Kāmika's Pūrvabhāga devotes many chapters to them.
notes: U58 owns Vāstu/Śilpa; here the ritual frame.

name: The three gifts (sopādhi, nirupādhi, sahaja dāna)
method_summary: Giving with a purpose, giving without a purpose, and innate (natural) giving — the last three sub-sthalas of the bhakta-sthala; skill in pure, innate giving marks the passage to māheśvara.

name: Austerity of body, speech and mind
method_summary: Bodily austerity: worship of gods, the twice-born, teachers and the wise; purity, uprightness, celibacy, non-harm. Verbal: speech that does not agitate, true, pleasant and beneficial, and recitation of scripture. Mental: serenity, gentleness, silence, self-restraint, purity of being — practised with faith and without desire for fruit (17.14–17).

warnings.text: Terrible austerities not enjoined by scripture, done with hypocrisy and egoism, tormenting the elements of the body and the Lord within, are demonic.
Austerity done with foolish obstinacy, by torturing oneself or to harm another, is tāmasic.

name: Pilgrimage (tīrthāṭana)
method_summary: Visiting sacred places: the Goddess's seats listed in the Devī Gītā, and pilgrimage among the Uddhava Gītā's niyamas; the Avadhūta Gītā's apology notes that pilgrimage presupposes a limit to the all-pervading.

name: Pilgrimage to tīrthas
method_summary: Journeying to holy places, bathing, worship, gifts and śrāddha there; seven cities give liberation; the inner meaning is purity of mind and the company of the holy, who themselves make places holy.

warnings.text: The greedy, cruel and hypocritical remain impure though they bathe in every tīrtha.

alt_method_summary: The Āraṇyakaparvan's pilgrimage to the tīrthas; Vidura's inner reading: the self is a river whose fords are sacred, whose water is truth, banks steadfastness and waves self-restraint — bathing in it purifies (MBh 5.40.19).
notes: U05's contribution; the Āraṇyaka's tīrtha lists are not itemized here.

name: Tirumūlar's eightfold yoga
method_summary: Tirumūlar's eight limbs — restraints, observances, posture, breath control, withdrawal, holding, meditation, absorption — taught to preserve the body as the vessel of realization and to reach Śiva within; summary only.

warnings.text: Breath retention and advanced practices are to be learned only from a guru (general teaching of the text; specific verses not recorded here).

name: Recitation and contemplation of the tirumantra
method_summary: Repetition of 'oṃ namo nārāyaṇāya', received at initiation, with contemplation of its meaning: the soul belongs to the Lord alone, not to itself, and seeks only his service.

name: Singing the Tirumuṟai (paṇṇicai)
method_summary: Singing the Tēvāram and other Tirumuṟai hymns in their melodic modes during temple worship and at home; the ōtuvār's office.

name: Daily home worship of the Lord (tiruvārādhanam)
method_summary: Worship of the Lord's image (arcā) at home each day, with purification, meditation on the teachers, offerings of water, flowers, food, recitation and prostration, done as service and not for any fruit.

name: The Mārkaḻi dawn vow (Tiruvempāvai nōṉpu)
method_summary: In the month of Mārkaḻi, rising before dawn, bathing and singing the Tiruvempāvai and Tiruppaḷḷiyeḻucci.

name: Tripuṇḍra (three lines of ash)
method_summary: Ash taken with the five brahma-mantras and applied in three horizontal lines, each line standing for a fire, a letter of Oṃ, a guṇa, a world, a power, a Veda and a deity (Kālāgnirudra); for all four stages of life.

name: Service of tulasī
method_summary: Watering, circumambulating and worshipping the tulasī plant, beloved of Kṛṣṇa, and wearing and chanting on tulasī beads.

name: Uccāra: contemplation of the breath (āṇava means)
method_summary: Āṇava contemplation of the vital breath in its five forms as it moves between the heart, the object and the dvādaśānta, recognizing seven successive blisses - one's own, the bliss-less, supreme, Brahman's, great, of consciousness and of the world (TĀ 5.43-52).
signs_of_progress: the seven ānandas; the five signs (ānanda, udbhava, kampa, nidrā, ghūrṇi) of TĀ 5.101-111

name: Udakakarma (water-offerings for the dead)
method_summary: Relatives offer water (with sesame) to the deceased after the cremation and during the days of impurity; not done for infants under two (YS 3.1).

name: Meditation on the udgītha
method_summary: Venerate the syllable Om as the udgītha, the highest essence, and the udgītha as the breath in the mouth untouched by evil; what is done with knowledge, faith and the upaniṣad is more powerful (ChU 1.1-1.12; BAU 1.3).

name: Living by gleaning (uñchavṛtti)
method_summary: The ascetic livelihood of gleaning grain left in the fields, praised in the Mokṣadharma and in the mongoose's story, where the gleaner's gift of his last food outweighs a great sacrifice (MBh 14.92–93; 12.184.18; 12.340–353).

name: Wandering alone like a madman
method_summary: Having closed the doors of the senses with the intellect, he wanders alone as if mad, taking discarded food; people call him mad and foolish. Kauṇḍinya: the madness is a feint to delude worldly examiners.

name: Upakosala's meditation (upakosala-vidyā)
method_summary: Venerate breath, joy (ka) and space (kha) as brahman, the fires as its forms, and the person seen in the eye as the self, the immortal, the fearless, brahman; the knower goes by the path of light and does not return.
notes: Upaniṣadic 'vidyā' (meditation-knowledge); the Brahma Sūtra (3.3) discusses which vidyās are to be combined.

name: Upanayana (initiation into Vedic study)
method_summary: The boy asks to become a student; the teacher takes his hand, invests him with girdle (of muñja grass for a brāhmaṇa), staff, deerskin and (later) sacred thread, and teaches him the Sāvitrī; he is now 'twice-born' with the Sāvitrī as mother and teacher as father. Due at eight, eleven or twelve years for the three classes (ŚB 11.5.4; ĀśGS 1.19–22; MDh 2.36–40; 2.169–171).

name: Ūrdhvapuṇḍra (vertical Vaiṣṇava mark)
method_summary: Vertical marks of gopīcandana clay applied with mantras at twelve places (householder) or fewer (students, forest-dwellers, ascetics; the paramahaṃsa one on the forehead) (Vāsudeva).

name: Wearing the upright mark (tirumaṇ)
method_summary: Daily application of the vertical white clay mark with the central line for Śrī on the forehead and body, a sign of belonging to the Lord.

name: The upright mark in gopīcandana
method_summary: Marking the forehead (and body) with the upright Vaiṣṇava mark in gopīcandana clay, praised as purifying and required for rites to bear fruit.

name: Yogic departure at death
method_summary: The yogin, choosing the time of death, withdraws the mind, restrains the breaths and leaves the body through the crown, either for immediate liberation or for the gradual ascent (BhP 2.2.15-31). Summary only.

warnings.text: Addressed to the accomplished yati; the Vāyavīya asks how the practiser who dies before completing yoga avoids becoming a self-killer (ātmahā).

alt_method_summary: Lineage contribution (Upaniṣadic): at death one goes up through the channel to the crown and reaches immortality (KU 2.3.16; ChU 8.6.6); saying 'Om' one rises by the sun's rays (ChU 8.6.5); the person made of mind goes out through the indrayoni (TU 1.6); through the suṣumṇā joined with breath, Om and mind one goes upward (MaiU 6.21). Summary only.

name: Discussion for truth (vāda)
method_summary: Examining a question with a partner by thesis and counter-thesis, proving and refuting only with the means of knowledge and tarka, within accepted tenets, in the five-membered form, aiming at ascertainment rather than victory.
prerequisites: knowledge of the means of knowledge and of the members
signs_of_progress: ascertainment (nirṇaya)
cutting of doubts

name: Debate for determining the truth (vāda)
method_summary: Debate aimed only at ascertaining the truth, as between teacher and disciple, following the rules of the Kathālakṣaṇa; the maṭhas continue the practice in scholarly disputations.
notes: The maṭha disputations (e.g. during the Cāturmāsya) are recalled, not verified.

name: Cutting the flows (vāhaccheda)
method_summary: Arresting the left and right currents of breath at the heart, as taught by Kṣemarāja, by the silent utterance of vowelless sounds, so that the centre opens (Kṣemarāja's auto-commentary on Pratyabhijñāhṛdaya 18; summary, no method given here).

name: Rule-based devotional practice (vaidhī sādhana)
method_summary: Performing the limbs of devotion — hearing, chanting, worship, fasts, vows — because scripture commands them, under a guru, until spontaneous attraction arises.

name: Dispassion (vairāgya)
method_summary: Turning away from objects by seeing the faults of acquiring, guarding, losing, attachment and harm (external dispassion), and seeing even pradhāna as like a dream or magic show (internal dispassion); with practice, a support of meditation.
signs_of_progress: calming of passion; freedom from expectation (like Piṅgalā, SS 4.11)

warnings.text: Through dispassion (alone) comes absorption into prakṛti, not liberation.
External contentment from abstaining from objects, without knowledge of the principles, does not liberate.

alt_method_summary: Cultivating freedom from thirst for objects seen and heard of in scripture, by seeing their faults through reflection (1.15, YBh 1.15); higher dispassion, from discernment of the puruṣa, is freedom from thirst for the guṇas (1.16); dispassion even toward the highest powers yields kaivalya (3.50).

name: Observances for the unseen (Vaiśeṣika)
method_summary: Ablution, fasting, celibacy, residence in the teacher's household, forest-dwelling, sacrifice, giving, sprinkling, and observances regarding directions, lunar mansions, mantras and times — undertaken for the unseen result (adṛṣṭa).

warnings.text: Fasting is listed without further prescription; no durations are given in the sūtra (prolonged fasting is not described here).

name: Yoga: the mind abiding in the self (Vaiśeṣika)
method_summary: Withdrawing the mind from contact with the senses so that it abides in the self, where the embodied one has neither pleasure nor pain; through a particular conjunction of self and mind the yogin perceives the self.
signs_of_progress: absence of pleasure and pain while embodied
perception of the self

name: Vaiṣṇavī mudrā
method_summary: The inner target held while the gaze is outward and unblinking (Śāṇḍilya 1.31); in the Nādabindu, the seal held while listening to the inner sound in the right ear.

name: Meditation on the self common to all men (vaiśvānara-vidyā)
method_summary: Venerate the vaiśvānara self as the whole — sky as head, sun as eye, wind as breath, space as trunk, water as bladder, earth as feet — 'a span in size and beyond measure', not as any one of its parts; the first morsels of food are then offered into it as an agnihotra.

warnings.text: Each partial meditation is incomplete, and the king says each would have come to harm (losing head, sight, breath...) without the whole teaching (ChU 5.12-17).

notes: Upaniṣadic 'vidyā' (meditation-knowledge); the Brahma Sūtra (3.3) discusses which vidyās are to be combined.

name: Vājapeya
method_summary: A soma rite of 'the drink of strength', with a chariot race, granting pre-eminence.

name: Vajrolī, amarolī, sahajolī
method_summary: Named in the Yogatattva among haṭha practices concerned with retaining bindu; recorded by name only.

warnings.text: Union with women causes loss of bindu; the yogin should avoid their company.

name: Varṇa: the letters and resonance in the āṇava means
method_summary: Āṇava immersion through the 'letter' (varṇa) - the unstruck resonance and seed-syllables contemplated with the breath (TĀ 5).

name: Placing the letters and forms of Viṣṇu (nyāsa)
method_summary: Placing on one's body the fifty letters as the fifty forms of Viṣṇu (Aja, Ānanda, Indra ...) and the parts of the mantras, as part of worship.

equivalents.note: Dvaita's nyāsa places forms of Viṣṇu, not Śākta or Śaiva deities.

prerequisites: dīkṣā

name: Destruction of latent tendencies (vāsanā-kṣaya)
method_summary: Weakening impure tendencies (attachment, pride, the three vāsanās) by cultivating their opposites and pure tendencies, until even these are let go; practised with knowledge and dissolution of mind.

name: Weakening latent tendencies
method_summary: First replacing dark, object-bound tendencies with pure ones such as friendliness, then giving up all tendencies and even the desire for liberation.

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 1: Fullness at the two points where the breath arises
method_summary: The supreme [Goddess], whose nature is emission (visarga), sounds forth as prāṇa above and as jīva (the in-breath) below; by dwelling on and filling the two places where they arise, the state of fullness (bharitā sthiti) comes about.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).
notes: Verses 24 (KSTS 8 / GRETIL numbering). Commentators identify the two places as the heart and the dvādaśānta (Kaumudī: 'utpattau dvādaśānte dvitīye hṛdi'). First dhāraṇā in Ānandabhaṭṭa's count as well.

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 10: The same method on a void, a wall or a worthy vessel
method_summary: By this very method, contemplation on anything whatever - on a void, on a wall, on an excellent person (pātra) - dissolves of itself and grants the boon.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).
notes: Verses 33 (KSTS 8 / GRETIL numbering).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 100: Neither attachment nor aversion
method_summary: One should not cultivate aversion anywhere, nor attachment anywhere; in the middle, free of attachment and aversion, Brahman spreads.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).
notes: Verses 126 (KSTS 8 / GRETIL numbering).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 101: The unknowable and the void as Bhairava
method_summary: What is unknowable, ungraspable, void, what lies in non-being - all that is to be contemplated as Bhairava; at its end, awakening arises.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).
notes: Verses 127 (KSTS 8 / GRETIL numbering).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 102: The mind in outer space
method_summary: Placing the mind in outer space - eternal, supportless, void, pervasive, free of limitation - one enters the spaceless.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).
notes: Verses 128 (KSTS 8 / GRETIL numbering).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 103: Letting go of each object the moment the mind goes to it
method_summary: Wherever the mind goes, abandoning that very thing at that very moment, by not letting it settle, one becomes waveless.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).
notes: Verses 129 (KSTS 8 / GRETIL numbering).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 104: Continuous utterance of the word 'Bhairava'
method_summary: 'He makes all resound through fear (bhayā ... ravayati), he gives all, he pervades the whole' - by continuously uttering the word 'Bhairava' [with this sense], one becomes Śiva.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).
notes: Verses 130 (KSTS 8 / GRETIL numbering).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 105: At the thought 'I' and 'mine'
method_summary: When notions such as 'I', 'this is mine' arise, the mind goes to the supportless; impelled by meditation on that, one becomes calm.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).
notes: Verses 131 (KSTS 8 / GRETIL numbering).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 106: Contemplating the words 'eternal', 'all-pervading', 'supportless'
method_summary: Meditating at every moment on the words 'eternal', 'all-pervading', 'supportless', 'pervasive', 'lord of all', according to their meaning, one attains one's aim.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).
notes: Verses 132 (KSTS 8 / GRETIL numbering).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 107: 'What reality has a magic show?'
method_summary: 'All this, without reality, stands like a magic show; what reality has a magic show?' - by firmness in this, one goes to peace.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).
notes: Verses 133 (KSTS 8 / GRETIL numbering). Illusion imagery used as a contemplation; relevant to the Advaita/Śaiva dispute on the world.

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 108: The unchanging self: the world as void
method_summary: For the unchanging self, where is knowledge, where is action? External things depend on knowledge; therefore this world is void.

prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).
notes: Verses 111 (KSTS 8 / GRETIL numbering).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 87: When the mind's supports fail
method_summary: When, through incapacity or ignorance regarding the supports (objects), or through the dissolution of the mind, absorption into the power has arisen, at the end of its agitation [appears] the form of Bhairava.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).
notes: Verses 112 (KSTS 8 / GRETIL numbering). Obscure; readings differ ('śaktyā ... dhyānāt' in the Kaumudī). Low confidence.

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 88: The sampradāya: fixed eyes; closed ears and lower door
method_summary: Hear, O Goddess, this traditional teaching (sampradāya), which I declare fully: isolation (kaivalya) arises at once when the eyes are merely held still (113). Contracting the ears and likewise the lower door, meditating on the vowelless and consonantless, one enters the eternal Brahman (114).
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).
notes: Verses 113-114 (KSTS 8 / GRETIL numbering). Grouped: v. 114 is absent from the Kaumudī recension's main text and is reported after the 'sampradāya' verse in one manuscript.

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 89: Looking down into a well or deep pit
method_summary: Standing above a well or a great pit and gazing down, for one whose mind is free of thought-constructs, the mind dissolves at once, clearly.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).
notes: Verses 115 (KSTS 8 / GRETIL numbering).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 9: The five voids like the eyes of a peacock's feather
method_summary: For one who meditates on the five voids as [like] the variegated circles on a peacock's feathers, entry into the heart, the unsurpassed void, takes place.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).
notes: Verses 32 (KSTS 8 / GRETIL numbering). The 'five voids' are read by commentators as the five sense-faculties or five elements (interpretation).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 90: Wherever the mind goes, there is Śiva
method_summary: Wherever the mind goes, outside or within, there is the state of Śiva; since it is all-pervading, where could [the mind] go?
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).
notes: Verses 116 (KSTS 8 / GRETIL numbering).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 91: Consciousness shining through each sense
method_summary: Wherever, through the path of the senses, the consciousness of the all-pervading one is manifested, since it has the nature of that alone, by dissolution in consciousness there is fullness.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).
notes: Verses 117 (KSTS 8 / GRETIL numbering).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 92: Sneeze, fear, grief, flight, curiosity, hunger
method_summary: At the beginning and end of a sneeze, in fear, in grief, in a deep cave (or: in sobbing), when fleeing from battle, in curiosity, at the beginning and end of hunger, there is a state full of the being of Brahman.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).
notes: Verses 118 (KSTS 8 / GRETIL numbering). Compare Spandakārikā 1.22 (spanda found in intense states).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 93: Letting go of remembered objects and places
method_summary: When things are remembered, or a place is seen, one should let the mind go from it; making one's body supportless, the Lord spreads forth.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).
notes: Verses 119 (KSTS 8 / GRETIL numbering).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 94: Slowly withdrawing the gaze from an object
method_summary: Having placed the gaze on some object, one should slowly withdraw it; that knowledge, together with the mind, O Goddess, becomes an abode of the void.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).
notes: Verses 120 (KSTS 8 / GRETIL numbering).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 95: The understanding born of intense devotion
method_summary: The kind of understanding that arises in one who is dispassionate through the intensity of devotion - that is the eternal power of Śaṅkara; one should contemplate it; from that, [one is] Śiva.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).
notes: Verses 121 (KSTS 8 / GRETIL numbering).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 96: The voidness of all else when one object is known
method_summary: When one particular object is being known, there is voidness with regard to all other objects; meditating with the mind on that very [voidness], even while knowing, one becomes tranquil.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).
notes: Verses 122 (KSTS 8 / GRETIL numbering).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 97: Purity and impurity
method_summary: The purity prescribed by those of little knowledge is [regarded as] impurity in the vision of Śambhu; [in truth] nothing is pure or impure; therefore, free of thought-constructs, one becomes happy.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).
notes: Verses 123 (KSTS 8 / GRETIL numbering). The GRETIL e-text reads 'sā śuddhiḥ'; the usual reading is 'sā 'śuddhiḥ' (impurity). Linked to the dispute on ritual purity.

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 98: Bhairava in ordinary things
method_summary: Bhairava is present everywhere as being, even in ordinary things; and there is nothing beyond it other than that - this is the non-dual way.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).
notes: Verses 124 (KSTS 8 / GRETIL numbering).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 99: Equality toward friend and foe
method_summary: Equal toward enemy and friend, equal in honour and dishonour - knowing [this] because Brahman is completely full, one becomes happy.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).
notes: Verses 125 (KSTS 8 / GRETIL numbering).

name: Vedic study (vedādhyayana / svādhyāya)
method_summary: Learning one's own Vedic recension by recitation from a teacher, as enjoined by 'one's own Veda is to be studied'; in the Mīmāṃsā account it precedes, and makes possible, the inquiry into the meaning of Vedic sentences.
prerequisites: initiation into Vedic study (upanayana), per Dharmaśāstra

name: Vedic recitation (vedapāṭha, svādhyāya of the Saṃhitā)
method_summary: Learning and reciting one's śākhā's Saṃhitā orally from the teacher's mouth, phrase by phrase, with exact accents marked by hand movements, first in the continuous form, then word by word and in the interwoven recitations; daily recitation of the Veda is itself counted a sacrifice (brahmayajña). The Soma book says whoever studies the purifying verses eats purified food (RV 9.67.31).
prerequisites: upanayana (initiation) by a teacher of the śākhā
duration: years of daily study; the complete Saṃhitā with its modified recitations traditionally takes a decade or more (as reported; low confidence)
signs_of_progress: mastery of the Saṃhitā, then pada, krama and the vikṛtis
the six virtues of a reciter (sweetness, distinctness, word-division, accent, composure, tempo)

warnings.text: A mantra wrong in accent or letter does not convey its meaning; as a verbal thunderbolt it harms the sacrificer, as 'Indra-śatru' did through a fault of accent.
One who recites the Veda without understanding its meaning is a post bearing a load; what is repeated without understanding never blazes, like dry fuel without fire.
Studying without the hand-gestures, lacking accent and letters, one is 'burned' by the Ṛg, Yajus and Sāman.

name: Breath-control with Oṃ, the utterances and the Gāyatrī
method_summary: Breath-control performed while mentally reciting the Gāyatrī with its 'head', preceded by the utterances and with Oṃ, as part of the twilight worship and as the renouncer's austerity; it burns away the faults of the senses (MDh 6.70–72; YS 1.23; VDh 10.5).
notes: No retention counts or durations are recorded here.

name: The Vedic recitations (pāṭha): continuous, word-by-word, step and the eight modified ones
method_summary: The pupil learns the text orally from the teacher in the continuous form (saṃhitā), word by word (pada), in overlapping pairs (krama) and in the elaborate 'modified' patterns (jaṭā, ghana and others), with exact accent and quantity, pronouncing each sound 'as a tigress carries her cubs' (PŚ 25) and avoiding the six faults of reciters (PŚ 32).

warnings.text: A mantra faulty in accent or sound harms the sacrificer (PŚ 52).
Reciting without understanding is 'dry fuel without fire' (Nirukta 1.18).

name: Night rite in the great cremation ground (literary)
method_summary: Summary only: in Bāṇa's Harṣacarita the Śaiva adept Bhairavācārya performs a mantra-rite at night in the great cremation ground, guarded by the king and disciples.
notes: Named 'vetāla-sādhana' in scholarship; the text's details were not checked in this run.

name: Wearing sacred ash (vibhūti) and tripuṇḍra
method_summary: Applying ash consecrated with 'namaḥ śivāya' as three horizontal lines on the forehead and fifteen places of the body; one of the eight shields.

name: Inquiry (vicāra) as the Yoga Vāsiṣṭha teaches
method_summary: Reflecting, with scripture and the wise, on 'who am I? what is this world?', discriminating the Self from body, senses and mind until the seen is known not to exist apart from consciousness; Cūḍālā's daily self-questioning is the model.

equivalents.note: related to the later practice of self-inquiry (recent teachers); not asserted identical

name: Renunciation of the knower (vidvat-sannyāsa)
method_summary: Renunciation by one who has attained knowledge, as the natural expression and protection of liberation while living (the paramahaṃsa life).

name: Observance of the Vidyāpīṭha adept (vidyāvrata)
method_summary: The Vidyāpīṭha sādhaka, to master a goddess-mantra, lives in Kāpālika style — cremation ground, skull-bowl, offerings to yoginīs — for a fixed period. Recorded as summary only; no procedures.

warnings.text: Lakṣmīdhara (a Samaya critic) condemns the Kāpālika and left-hand tantras as deceiving and far from the Vedic path.

notes: Sexual and impure-substance rites of the Yāmala tantras are not described (restricted).

name: Vidyārambha (beginning of letters)
method_summary: Beginning the learning of the alphabet, a later addition to the lists.

name: Dissolution of thought-constructs (vikalpakṣaya)
method_summary: Letting thought-constructs subside by fixing awareness at the heart and not thinking of anything, one comes to rest in the thought-free centre (Kṣemarāja's auto-commentary on Pratyabhijñāhṛdaya 18; summary).

name: The eight modified recitations (vikṛti)
method_summary: Jaṭā, mālā, śikhā, rekhā, dhvaja, daṇḍa, ratha and ghana: permutations built on the krama that lock the order of every word of the text.
notes: List as traditionally given; the source ascription is low-confidence.

name: Viparītakaraṇī (the inverted practice)
method_summary: An inverted posture-seal named in the Yogatattva; the text warns that the practitioner must then eat sufficiently or the fire consumes the body.

warnings.text: The practitioner must eat plenty, otherwise the fire quickly consumes the body.

name: The Virajā initiation (Śiva Gītā)
method_summary: An initiation with sacred ash and the Virajā mantras, taking the Pāśupata vow, before worship of Śiva.

name: Hospitality (viruntōmpal)
method_summary: Receiving and feeding guests as the purpose of the householder's life.

name: Concentration giving rise to subtle sense-perception (1.35)
method_summary: Concentrating on the tip of the nose, tip, middle and root of the tongue, or the palate, until divine smell, taste, touch, sound or form is perceived; such experiences bind the mind to steadiness and confirm what scripture and the teacher say (YBh 1.35).
signs_of_progress: awareness of divine smell, taste, form, touch or sound (YBh 1.35)

name: Viśeṣa-dīkṣā
method_summary: The 'special' initiation that qualifies the initiate for the regular worship of Śiva (content varies among manuals).

name: Worship of Viṣṇu according to the Tantrasārasaṅgraha and Yogadīpikā
method_summary: Daily and occasional worship of Viṣṇu (and his forms, especially Kṛṣṇa, Narasiṃha and Rāma) with mantras derived from the praṇava, placing of letters and forms on the body, purifications, invocation into the image and offerings, remembering that Hari in the worshipper and Hari in the image is the one Lord who accepts the worship.
prerequisites: dīkṣā

name: Recitation of the thousand names of Viṣṇu
method_summary: Reciting the thousand names of Viṣṇu taught by Bhīṣma, which frees from the bondage of saṃsāra and from fear (MBh 13.135).

name: Prenatal offering to Viṣṇu (viṣṇubali)
method_summary: A saṃskāra performed during pregnancy (the eighth month) dedicating the unborn child to Viṣṇu, on which the Vaikhānasa claim to be Vaiṣṇavas from the womb rests.

name: The sorrowless, luminous activity (1.36)
method_summary: Concentrating on the lotus of the heart until the luminous buddhi appears like the light of sun, moon, planets and gems; or absorbing the mind in I-am-ness until it is calm and endless like a waveless ocean (YBh 1.36).
signs_of_progress: luminous appearances; 'I am' alone (YBh 1.36)

name: Viśvajit (the rite of giving away all)
method_summary: A rite in which the sacrificer gives away all he owns; no fruit is stated, so heaven is understood (MS 4.3.15); what one is master of is given, but not the land, which is common to all (MS 6.7.1–3).

name: Mind on one free of passion (1.37)
method_summary: Letting the mind take as its support the mind of one free of passion (1.37, YBh 1.37).

name: Vivāha (marriage)
method_summary: The householder's sacrament, following regional and village custom (ĀśGS 1.7.1): the taking of the bride's hand, circling the fire, stepping on the stone, the seven steps, and establishing the domestic fire; eight forms of marriage are recognized (MDh 3.21).

name: Cultivating discriminative discernment (viveka-khyāti)
method_summary: Cultivating the cognition of the difference between sattva and puruṣa until it is unwavering, false knowledge burnt like a seed (2.26, YBh 2.26); the practice of the limbs makes knowledge shine up to it (2.28).
signs_of_progress: the sevenfold final insight (2.27); the mind bends toward kaivalya (4.26)

warnings.text: In its gaps other cognitions ('I am', 'mine') arise from impressions; they are removed like the afflictions.

name: Renunciation of the seeker (vividiṣā-sannyāsa)
method_summary: Formal renunciation of rites and possessions by one who desires knowledge, to devote oneself wholly to hearing and the rest.
prerequisites: dispassion

name: Circumambulation of Vraja (vraja-parikramā)
method_summary: Pilgrimage around the sites of Kṛṣṇa's play in Braj (Govardhana, Rādhākuṇḍa, the forests), done by Gauḍīyas and the Puṣṭimārga (whose ban-yātrā follows Vallabha's seats); residence in Vraja is one of the five potent limbs.

name: Vows (vrata)
method_summary: Observances for a lunar day or a period - fasting, vigil, worship, recitation and gifts - dedicated to a deity, with a story and a promised fruit.
notes: Prolonged fasts (e.g. month-long regimens) are restricted content and are not detailed here.

name: Vrātyastoma (rites for admitting Vrātyas)
method_summary: Soma rites by which groups living outside the sacrificial order are made fit to sacrifice (PB 17.1–4).

name: Release of a bull (vṛṣotsarga)
method_summary: On the eleventh day a consecrated bull is set free for the dead; without it the preta state becomes fixed.

name: Meditation on the vyāhṛtis
method_summary: Meditate on bhūḥ, bhuvaḥ, suvaḥ and mahaḥ as the worlds, lights, Vedas and breaths, mahaḥ being brahman, the self (TU 1.5-6).

name: Sacrifice performed as duty (yajña)
method_summary: Perform sacrifice according to injunction, without desire for fruit, with the resolve 'it ought to be done' (17.11), for the sake of which action does not bind (3.9); in the widened sense, the sacrifices of austerity, yoga, study, sense-restraint, breath and knowledge (4.25–33).

warnings.text: Sacrifice contrary to injunction, without distribution of food, mantras, priests' fees and faith is tāmasic.

notes: U05's contribution; Vedic ritual is covered by U01–U02.
alt_method_summary: The principal enjoined act: offering a substance with reference to a deity named in the injunction or mantra, with its subsidiaries in fixed sequence; it produces the apūrva that yields the fruit.

name: The restraints (yama)
method_summary: Keeping non-harming, truthfulness, non-stealing, celibacy and non-possessiveness (2.30), without limitation of class, place, time or occasion — the great vow (2.31); non-harming is the root of all (YBh 2.30).
signs_of_progress: the fruits of 2.35–39

name: Meditation on whatever is agreeable (1.39)
method_summary: Meditating on whatever object one finds agreeable; the mind stable there becomes stable elsewhere too (1.39, YBh 1.39).
signs_of_progress: mastery from the smallest to the greatest (1.40)

name: Worship of the divine couple (yugala-upāsanā)
method_summary: Worship and meditation on Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa together — Rādhā on Kṛṣṇa's left, served by the sakhīs — in the Nimbārka school, with Braj songs of the couple's play (Yugalaśataka, Mahāvāṇī).
